CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_NOTIFICATION_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CloudFormation stack with no NotificationARNs configured, or whose NotificationARNs do not match the optional snsTopic1-snsTopic5 parameters.
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_NOTIFICATION_CHECK.condition_logic: len(cloudformation.Stack.NotificationARNs) > 0 AND (snsTopic1..snsTopic5 == null OR cloudformation.Stack.NotificationARNs contains snsTopicN)
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_NOTIFICATION_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your CloudFormation stacks send event notifications to an Amazon SNS topic. Optionally checks if specified Amazon SNS topics are used. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if CloudFormation stacks do not send notifications.
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_NOTIFICATION_CHECK.remediation_summary: Update each CloudFormation stack to publish events to one or more SNS topics by setting NotificationARNs via aws cloudformation update-stack --notification-arns <topic-arn>, or Terraform aws_cloudformation_stack.notification_arns = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]. Subscribe operations / security teams to those topics.
CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_NOTIFICATION_CHECK.title: CloudFormation stacks must publish events to an SNS topic

CLOUDFRONT_ACCESSLOGS_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose Logging.Enabled is false, and optionally whose log bucket does not match S3BucketName.
CLOUDFRONT_ACCESSLOGS_ENABLED.condition_logic: cloudfront.Distribution.Logging.Enabled == true AND (S3BucketName == null OR cloudfront.Distribution.Logging.Bucket == S3BucketName)
CLOUDFRONT_ACCESSLOGS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudFront distributions are configured to deliver access logs to an Amazon S3 bucket using standard logging (legacy). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a CloudFront distribution does not have legacy logging configured.
CLOUDFRONT_ACCESSLOGS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable standard (legacy) access logging on each CloudFront distribution, pointing it at a dedicated S3 bucket via aws cloudfront update-distribution with Logging.Enabled = true and Bucket / Prefix set, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.logging_config { include_cookies = false bucket = "<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com" prefix = "cf-logs/" }.
CLOUDFRONT_ACCESSLOGS_ENABLED.title: CloudFront distributions must have access logging enabled

CLOUDFRONT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution not associated with a WAF or WAFv2 web ACL, or whose web ACL ID/ARN is not in wafWebAclIds.
CLOUDFRONT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF.condition_logic: cloudfront.Distribution.WebAclId != null AND (wafWebAclIds == null OR cloudfront.Distribution.WebAclId IN wafWebAclIds)
CLOUDFRONT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudFront distributions are associated with either web application firewall (WAF) or WAFv2 web access control lists (ACLs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a CloudFront distribution is not associated with a WAF web ACL.
CLOUDFRONT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF.remediation_summary: Set the WebACLId (WAFv2 ARN, including CLOUDFRONT scope) on each CloudFront distribution via aws cloudfront update-distribution --web-acl-id <arn>, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.web_acl_id = aws_wafv2_web_acl.cf.arn. Restrict to ARNs in wafWebAclIds when configured.
CLOUDFRONT_ASSOCIATED_WITH_WAF.title: CloudFront distributions must be associated with an AWS WAF web ACL

CLOUDFRONT_CUSTOM_SSL_CERTIFICATE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose ViewerCertificate.CloudFrontDefaultCertificate is true (i.e., it is using the default *.cloudfront.net certificate). Multi-tenant distributions are not applicable.
CLOUDFRONT_CUSTOM_SSL_CERTIFICATE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the certificate associated with an Amazon CloudFront distribution is the default SSL certificate. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a CloudFront distribution uses the default SSL certificate. Multi-tenant distributions are not applicable.
CLOUDFRONT_CUSTOM_SSL_CERTIFICATE.remediation_summary: Provision an ACM certificate in us-east-1 for the distribution's alternate domain names and attach it via aws cloudfront update-distribution with ViewerCertificate.AcmCertificateArn set and CloudFrontDefaultCertificate = false, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.viewer_certificate { acm_certificate_arn = ... ssl_support_method = "sni-only" minimum_protocol_version = "TLSv1.2_2021" }.
CLOUDFRONT_CUSTOM_SSL_CERTIFICATE.title: CloudFront distributions must use a custom SSL certificate

CLOUDFRONT_NO_DEPRECATED_SSL_PROTOCOLS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose CustomOriginConfig.OriginSslProtocols contains 'SSLv3'.
CLOUDFRONT_NO_DEPRECATED_SSL_PROTOCOLS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if CloudFront distributions are using deprecated SSL protocols for HTTPS communication between CloudFront edge locations and custom origins. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a CloudFront distribution if any 'OriginSslProtocols' includes 'SSLv3'.
CLOUDFRONT_NO_DEPRECATED_SSL_PROTOCOLS.remediation_summary: Remove SSLv3 from each custom origin's OriginSslProtocols, leaving only TLSv1.2 (or stronger) via aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.origin.custom_origin_config { origin_ssl_protocols = ["TLSv1.2"] }. Ensure the origin server itself supports TLS 1.2+.
CLOUDFRONT_NO_DEPRECATED_SSL_PROTOCOLS.title: CloudFront distributions must not use deprecated SSL protocols to origins

CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_ACCESS_IDENTITY_ENABLE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution backed by an S3 origin whose S3OriginConfig.OriginAccessIdentity is empty.
CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_ACCESS_IDENTITY_ENABLE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if CloudFront distribution with Amazon S3 Origin type has origin access identity configured. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the CloudFront distribution is backed by S3 and any origin type is not OAI configured, or the origin is not an S3 bucket.
CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_ACCESS_IDENTITY_ENABLE.remediation_summary: Create an Origin Access Identity (or, preferred, Origin Access Control) and attach it to every S3-backed origin via aws cloudfront create-cloud-front-origin-access-identity then aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_origin_access_identity + aws_cloudfront_distribution.origin.s3_origin_config.origin_access_identity. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant only that OAI s3:GetObject.
CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_ACCESS_IDENTITY_ENABLE.title: CloudFront S3 origins must have an origin access identity configured

CLOUDFRONT_S3_ORIGIN_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENAB.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution with an S3 origin whose OriginAccessControlId is empty.
CLOUDFRONT_S3_ORIGIN_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENAB.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) Origin type has origin access control (OAC) enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for CloudFront distributions with Amazon S3 origins that don't have OAC enabled.
CLOUDFRONT_S3_ORIGIN_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENAB.remediation_summary: Create an Origin Access Control (OAC) and attach it to every S3 origin via aws cloudfront create-origin-access-control followed by aws cloudfront update-distribution with origin.OriginAccessControlId set, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_origin_access_control + aws_cloudfront_distribution.origin.origin_access_control_id. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant SigV4 access to the distribution's service principal.
CLOUDFRONT_S3_ORIGIN_ACCESS_CONTROL_ENAB.title: CloudFront S3 origins must use origin access control (OAC)

CLOUDFRONT_SECURITY_POLICY_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose ViewerCertificate.MinimumProtocolVersion is below TLSv1.2_2018.
CLOUDFRONT_SECURITY_POLICY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudFront distributions are using a minimum security policy and cipher suite of TLSv1.2 or greater for viewer connections. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a CloudFront distribution if the minimumProtocolVersion is below TLSv1.2_2018.
CLOUDFRONT_SECURITY_POLICY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Set ViewerCertificate.MinimumProtocolVersion to TLSv1.2_2021 (or 2019/2018) via aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.viewer_certificate.minimum_protocol_version = "TLSv1.2_2021". This requires using a custom (non-default) ACM certificate.
CLOUDFRONT_SECURITY_POLICY_CHECK.title: CloudFront distributions must use TLSv1.2 or stronger for viewers

CLOUDFRONT_SNI_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution that uses a custom SSL certificate but has SslSupportMethod set to vip (dedicated IP) instead of sni-only.
CLOUDFRONT_SNI_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudFront distributions are using a custom SSL certificate and are configured to use SNI to serve HTTPS requests. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a custom SSL certificate is associated but the SSL support method is a dedicated IP address.
CLOUDFRONT_SNI_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Switch ViewerCertificate.SslSupportMethod to sni-only via aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.viewer_certificate.ssl_support_method = "sni-only". This avoids the cost and IP exhaustion of dedicated-IP custom SSL.
CLOUDFRONT_SNI_ENABLED.title: CloudFront distributions must use SNI for HTTPS

CLOUDFRONT_TRAFFIC_TO_ORIGIN_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose CustomOriginConfig.OriginProtocolPolicy is http-only, or is match-viewer while the cache behavior allows ViewerProtocolPolicy = allow-all.
CLOUDFRONT_TRAFFIC_TO_ORIGIN_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudFront distributions are encrypting traffic to custom origins. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'OriginProtocolPolicy' is 'http-only' or if 'OriginProtocolPolicy' is 'match-viewer' and 'ViewerProtocolPolicy' is 'allow-all'.
CLOUDFRONT_TRAFFIC_TO_ORIGIN_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Set OriginProtocolPolicy to https-only on every custom origin (or to match-viewer only when all viewer behaviors redirect or require HTTPS), via aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.origin.custom_origin_config.origin_protocol_policy = "https-only".
CLOUDFRONT_TRAFFIC_TO_ORIGIN_ENCRYPTED.title: CloudFront distributions must encrypt traffic to custom origins

CLOUDFRONT_VIEWER_POLICY_HTTPS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (US East 1 only) that fails any CloudFront distribution whose default cache behavior or any cache behavior has ViewerProtocolPolicy set to allow-all.
CLOUDFRONT_VIEWER_POLICY_HTTPS.condition_logic: defaultCacheBehavior.ViewerProtocolPolicy != 'allow-all' AND all(b in cacheBehaviors, b.ViewerProtocolPolicy != 'allow-all')
CLOUDFRONT_VIEWER_POLICY_HTTPS.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether your Amazon CloudFront distributions use HTTPS (directly or via a redirection). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the value of ViewerProtocolPolicy is set to 'allow-all' for the defaultCacheBehavior or for the CacheBehaviors.
CLOUDFRONT_VIEWER_POLICY_HTTPS.remediation_summary: Update each cache behavior to set ViewerProtocolPolicy to redirect-to-https or https-only, never allow-all, via aws cloudfront update-distribution, or Terraform aws_cloudfront_distribution.default_cache_behavior.viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https".
CLOUDFRONT_VIEWER_POLICY_HTTPS.title: CloudFront viewer policy must require HTTPS

CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that confirms at least one CloudTrail trail exists and is enabled in the account. Optional parameters narrow compliance to a specific S3 bucket, SNS topic, or CloudWatch Logs log group.
CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(cloudtrail.Trail) AND cloudtrail.Trail.IsLogging == true AND (s3BucketName == null OR Trail.S3BucketName == s3BucketName) AND (snsTopicArn == null OR Trail.SnsTopicArn == snsTopicArn) AND (cloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn == null OR Trail.CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn == cloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn)
CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS CloudTrail trail is enabled in your AWS account. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a trail is not enabled. Optionally, the rule checks a specific S3 bucket, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic, and CloudWatch log group.
CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Create or enable at least one CloudTrail trail in the account that captures management events. Use aws cloudtrail create-trail / start-logging or Terraform aws_cloudtrail to log to a designated S3 bucket and, where required, to the configured SNS topic and CloudWatch Logs log group.
CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.title: At least one CloudTrail trail must be enabled in the account

CLOUDTRAIL_S3_DATAEVENTS_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if there is no CloudTrail trail configured to log S3 data events for all buckets, or for the specific buckets in S3BucketNames.
CLOUDTRAIL_S3_DATAEVENTS_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(trail) AND trail.EventSelectors contains { DataResource.Type == 'AWS::S3::Object' AND (S3BucketNames == null OR DataResource.Values covers S3BucketNames) }
CLOUDTRAIL_S3_DATAEVENTS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if at least one AWS CloudTrail trail is logging Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) data events for all S3 buckets. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are trails or if no trails record S3 data events.
CLOUDTRAIL_S3_DATAEVENTS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Add an event selector that records read and write S3 data events on a CloudTrail trail, e.g. aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name <trail> --event-selectors '[{"DataResources":[{"Type":"AWS::S3::Object","Values":["arn:aws:s3:::"]}],"IncludeManagementEvents":true,"ReadWriteType":"All"}]', or Terraform aws_cloudtrail.event_selector { data_resource { type = "AWS::S3::Object" values = ["arn:aws:s3:::"] } }.
CLOUDTRAIL_S3_DATAEVENTS_ENABLED.title: CloudTrail must log S3 object-level data events

CLOUDTRAIL_SECURITY_TRAIL_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account unless at least one CloudTrail trail is multi-region, records global service events, has log file validation enabled, is encrypted with a KMS key, records both read and write management events, and excludes none of them.
CLOUDTRAIL_SECURITY_TRAIL_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(trail) WHERE trail.IsMultiRegionTrail == true AND trail.IncludeGlobalServiceEvents == true AND trail.LogFileValidationEnabled == true AND trail.KmsKeyId != null AND trail.EventSelectors covers ReadWriteType=='All' AND trail.EventSelectors.IncludeManagementEvents == true
CLOUDTRAIL_SECURITY_TRAIL_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks that there is at least one AWS CloudTrail trail defined with security best practices. This rule is COMPLIANT if there is at least one trail that meets all of the following: records global service events; is a multi-region trail; has Log file validation enabled; encrypted with a KMS key; records events for reads and writes; records management events; does not exclude any management events. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if no trails meet all of the criteria mentioned above.
CLOUDTRAIL_SECURITY_TRAIL_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Create or update one CloudTrail trail to meet every requirement: aws cloudtrail update-trail --is-multi-region-trail --include-global-service-events --enable-log-file-validation --kms-key-id <kms-arn> followed by aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors with ReadWriteType=All and IncludeManagementEvents=true. In Terraform use aws_cloudtrail with is_multi_region_trail, include_global_service_events, enable_log_file_validation, kms_key_id and an event_selector covering management events.
CLOUDTRAIL_SECURITY_TRAIL_ENABLED.title: Account must have a CloudTrail trail meeting all security best practices

CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_ACTION_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CloudWatch alarm missing required ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, or OK actions per the alarmActionRequired/insufficientDataActionRequired/okActionRequired flags, or whose actions do not match the supplied action1-action5 ARNs.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_ACTION_CHECK.condition_logic: (alarmActionRequired == false OR len(alarm.AlarmActions) > 0) AND (insufficientDataActionRequired == false OR len(alarm.InsufficientDataActions) > 0) AND (okActionRequired == false OR len(alarm.OKActions) > 0) AND (action1..action5 == null OR action_arn IN alarm.actions)
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_ACTION_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if CloudWatch alarms have an action configured for the ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, or OK state. Optionally checks if any actions match a named ARN. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there is no action specified for the alarm or optional parameter.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_ACTION_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure each CloudWatch alarm with at least one action for the required states (ALARM, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, and optionally OK). Use aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm with --alarm-actions/--ok-actions/--insufficient-data-actions or Terraform aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm.alarm_actions to add an SNS topic, Auto Scaling, or Systems Manager action ARN.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_ACTION_CHECK.title: CloudWatch alarms must have a configured action

CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_RESOURCE_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any resource of resourceType (EBS volume, EC2 instance, RDS DB cluster, or S3 bucket) that does not have a CloudWatch alarm configured for metricName.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_RESOURCE_CHECK.condition_logic: exists(cloudwatch.Alarm) WHERE Alarm.Namespace_for(resourceType) AND Alarm.MetricName == metricName AND Alarm.Dimensions covers resource.Id
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_RESOURCE_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a resource type has a CloudWatch alarm for the named metric. For resource type, you can specify EBS volumes, EC2 instances, Amazon RDS clusters, or S3 buckets. The rule is COMPLIANT if the named metric has a resource ID and CloudWatch alarm.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_RESOURCE_CHECK.remediation_summary: Create CloudWatch alarms for each resource of resourceType watching metricName via aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm with the resource's dimensions (e.g., InstanceId), or Terraform aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm with namespace, metric_name and dimensions matched to each resource. Wire the alarm actions to SNS or auto-remediation.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_RESOURCE_CHECK.title: Targeted resources must have a CloudWatch alarm for the named metric

CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_SETTINGS_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CloudWatch alarm whose MetricName matches metricName but whose period, statistic, comparisonOperator, threshold or evaluationPeriods do not match the supplied parameters.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_SETTINGS_CHECK.condition_logic: alarm.MetricName == metricName AND alarm.Period == period AND (statistic == null OR alarm.Statistic == statistic) AND (comparisonOperator == null OR alarm.ComparisonOperator == comparisonOperator) AND (threshold == null OR alarm.Threshold == threshold) AND (evaluationPeriods == null OR alarm.EvaluationPeriods == evaluationPeriods)
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_SETTINGS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether CloudWatch alarms with the given metric name have the specified settings.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_SETTINGS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Update each CloudWatch alarm matching metricName to the required period, statistic, comparisonOperator, threshold and evaluationPeriods using aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm, or Terraform aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm with matching arguments. Standardize alarm definitions in a module to avoid drift.
CLOUDWATCH_ALARM_SETTINGS_CHECK.title: CloudWatch alarms must use the required settings

CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Checks if Amazon CloudWatch Log Groups are encrypted with any AWS KMS key or a specified AWS KMS key Id. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a CloudWatch Log Group is not encrypted with a KMS key or is encrypted with a KMS key not supplied in the rule parameter. Identifier: CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED Resource Types: AWS::Logs::LogGroup Trigger type: Periodic AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: KmsKeyId (Optional) Type: String Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the ID for the KMS key that is used to encrypt the log group.
CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudWatch Log Groups are encrypted with any AWS KMS key or a specified AWS KMS key Id. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a CloudWatch Log Group is not encrypted with a KMS key or is encrypted with a KMS key not supplied in the rule parameter. Identifier: CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED Resource Types: AWS::Logs::LogGroup Trigger type: Periodic AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: KmsKeyId (Optional) Type: String Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the ID for the KMS key that is used to encrypt the log group.
CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
CLOUDWATCH_LOG_GROUP_ENCRYPTED.title: Cloudwatch Log Group Encrypted

CLOUD_TRAIL_CLOUD_WATCH_LOGS_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any CloudTrail trail whose CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn is empty or whose most recent CloudWatch Logs delivery is older than expectedDeliveryWindowAge hours.
CLOUD_TRAIL_CLOUD_WATCH_LOGS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS CloudTrail trails are configured to send logs to CloudWatch logs. The trail is NON_COMPLIANT if the CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn property of the trail is empty.
CLOUD_TRAIL_CLOUD_WATCH_LOGS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure each CloudTrail trail to deliver events to a CloudWatch Logs log group by attaching a CloudWatch Logs role and log group ARN via aws cloudtrail update-trail --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn / --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn or Terraform aws_cloudtrail.cloud_watch_logs_group_arn / cloud_watch_logs_role_arn.
CLOUD_TRAIL_CLOUD_WATCH_LOGS_ENABLED.title: CloudTrail trails must stream events to CloudWatch Logs

CLOUD_TRAIL_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any CloudTrail trail whose KmsKeyId is not defined (i.e., not configured for SSE-KMS log encryption).
CLOUD_TRAIL_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS CloudTrail is configured to use the server side encryption (SSE) AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption. The rule is COMPLIANT if the KmsKeyId is defined.
CLOUD_TRAIL_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure a customer-managed KMS key on every CloudTrail trail using aws cloudtrail update-trail --kms-key-id <key-arn>, or Terraform aws_cloudtrail.kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.cloudtrail.arn. Grant CloudTrail kms:GenerateDataKey* and kms:DescribeKey via the key policy and rotate the key via aws_kms_key.enable_key_rotation = true.
CLOUD_TRAIL_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.title: CloudTrail logs must be encrypted with a KMS key

CLOUD_TRAIL_LOG_FILE_VALIDATION_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any CloudTrail trail whose LogFileValidationEnabled is false, meaning log integrity digest files are not produced.
CLOUD_TRAIL_LOG_FILE_VALIDATION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS CloudTrail creates a signed digest file with logs. AWS recommends that the file validation must be enabled on all trails. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the validation is not enabled.
CLOUD_TRAIL_LOG_FILE_VALIDATION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable log file validation on every trail with aws cloudtrail update-trail --enable-log-file-validation, or Terraform aws_cloudtrail.enable_log_file_validation = true. Periodically verify with aws cloudtrail validate-logs.
CLOUD_TRAIL_LOG_FILE_VALIDATION_ENABLED.title: CloudTrail trails must have log file validation enabled

CMK_BACKING_KEY_ROTATION_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that verifies automatic backing-key rotation is enabled for each customer-managed AWS KMS key. Asymmetric, HMAC, imported-material, and custom-key-store KMS keys are out of scope because automatic rotation is not supported for them.
CMK_BACKING_KEY_ROTATION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if automatic key rotation is enabled for each key and matches to the key ID of the customer created AWS KMS key. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the AWS Config recorder role for a resource does not have the kms:DescribeKey permission.
CMK_BACKING_KEY_ROTATION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable automatic key rotation on customer-managed symmetric KMS keys via the KMS console (Key rotation tab), CLI (aws kms enable-key-rotation --key-id <id>), or Terraform aws_kms_key resource (enable_key_rotation = true). Ensure the AWS Config recorder role has kms:DescribeKey permission.
CMK_BACKING_KEY_ROTATION_ENABLED.title: Customer-managed KMS keys must have automatic key rotation enabled

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ARTIFACT_ENCRYPTION.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CodeBuild project whose primary or secondary artifact configurations have encryptionDisabled set to true.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ARTIFACT_ENCRYPTION.condition_logic: codebuild.Project.Artifacts.EncryptionDisabled == false AND all(s in codebuild.Project.SecondaryArtifacts, s.EncryptionDisabled == false)
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ARTIFACT_ENCRYPTION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS CodeBuild project has encryption enabled for all of its artifacts. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'encryptionDisabled' is set to 'true' for any primary or secondary (if present) artifact configurations.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ARTIFACT_ENCRYPTION.remediation_summary: Update each CodeBuild project so artifacts (and any secondaryArtifacts) have encryptionDisabled = false and a KMS key configured: aws codebuild update-project --project '{...,"artifacts":{"encryptionDisabled":false},...}', or Terraform aws_codebuild_project.artifacts { encryption_disabled = false } plus encryption_key.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ARTIFACT_ENCRYPTION.title: CodeBuild project artifacts must be encrypted

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED.condition_description: Checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has privileged mode enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a CodeBuild project if ‘privilegedMode’ is set to ‘true’. Identifier: CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::CodeBuild::Project Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Middle East (UAE), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), C
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has privileged mode enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a CodeBuild project if ‘privilegedMode’ is set to ‘true’. Identifier: CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::CodeBuild::Project Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Middle East (UAE), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), C
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT_PRIVILEGED.title: Codebuild Project Environment Privileged Check

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVVAR_AWSCRED_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a CodeBuild project if any environment variable named AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID or AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY is stored as PLAINTEXT instead of being sourced from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVVAR_AWSCRED_CHECK.condition_logic: NOT exists(env_var IN project.Environment.EnvironmentVariables WHERE env_var.Name in ['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID','AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY'] AND env_var.Type == 'PLAINTEXT')
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVVAR_AWSCRED_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the project contains environment variables AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT when the project environment variables contains plaintext credentials.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVVAR_AWSCRED_CHECK.remediation_summary: Remove plaintext AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables from the CodeBuild project. Use a CodeBuild service role for AWS access, or store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store and reference them with type SECRETS_MANAGER or PARAMETER_STORE via aws codebuild update-project or Terraform aws_codebuild_project.environment.environment_variable.type.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_ENVVAR_AWSCRED_CHECK.title: CodeBuild projects must not store AWS credentials as plaintext environment variables

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has at least one log option enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the status of all present log configurations is set to 'DISABLED'. Identifier: CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED Resource Types: AWS::CodeBuild::Project Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Mexico (Central), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Canada West (Calgary) Region Parameters: s3BucketNames (Optional) Type: String Comma-separated list of Amazon
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS CodeBuild project environment has at least one log option enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the status of all present log configurations is set to 'DISABLED'. Identifier: CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED Resource Types: AWS::CodeBuild::Project Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Mexico (Central), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Canada West (Calgary) Region Parameters: s3BucketNames (Optional) Type: String Comma-separated list of Amazon
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: Codebuild Project Logging Enabled

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_S3_LOGS_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CodeBuild project whose S3LogsConfig has encryptionDisabled = true, unless the project name appears in exemptedProjects.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_S3_LOGS_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a AWS CodeBuild project configured with Amazon S3 Logs has encryption enabled for its logs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'encryptionDisabled' is set to 'true' in a S3LogsConfig of a CodeBuild project.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_S3_LOGS_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Set logsConfig.s3Logs.encryptionDisabled to false on each CodeBuild project via aws codebuild update-project, or Terraform aws_codebuild_project.logs_config.s3_logs { encryption_disabled = false }. Exempt only project names listed in exemptedProjects.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_S3_LOGS_ENCRYPTED.title: CodeBuild project S3 logs must be encrypted

CODEBUILD_PROJECT_SOURCE_REPO_URL_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a CodeBuild project whose Bitbucket source repository URL contains embedded sign-in credentials (for example, a username:password segment).
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_SOURCE_REPO_URL_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Bitbucket source repository URL contains sign-in credentials or not. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the URL contains any sign-in information and COMPLIANT if it doesn't.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_SOURCE_REPO_URL_CHECK.remediation_summary: Remove embedded credentials from the Bitbucket source URL of the CodeBuild project. Connect the repository through OAuth, an AWS CodeStar connection, or an SSH access token, and update the source via aws codebuild update-project or Terraform aws_codebuild_project.source.location to a credential-free URL.
CODEBUILD_PROJECT_SOURCE_REPO_URL_CHECK.title: CodeBuild Bitbucket source URLs must not embed credentials

CODEDEPLOY_LAMBDA_ALLATONCE_TRAFFIC_SHIF.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CodeDeploy Lambda deployment group whose deploymentConfigName equals 'CodeDeployDefault.LambdaAllAtOnce'.
CODEDEPLOY_LAMBDA_ALLATONCE_TRAFFIC_SHIF.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the deployment group for Lambda Compute Platform is not using the default deployment configuration. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the deployment group is using the deployment configuration 'CodeDeployDefault.LambdaAllAtOnce'.
CODEDEPLOY_LAMBDA_ALLATONCE_TRAFFIC_SHIF.remediation_summary: Switch each Lambda deployment group to a Linear or Canary deployment config (e.g., CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes) via aws deploy update-deployment-group --deployment-config-name <name>, or Terraform aws_codedeploy_deployment_group.deployment_config_name. Use CloudWatch alarms for automatic rollback.
CODEDEPLOY_LAMBDA_ALLATONCE_TRAFFIC_SHIF.title: CodeDeploy Lambda deployments must avoid all-at-once traffic shifting

CODEPIPELINE_DEPLOYMENT_COUNT_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any CodePipeline whose first deployment stage performs more than one deployment, and optionally fails subsequent stages whose deployment count exceeds deploymentLimit.
CODEPIPELINE_DEPLOYMENT_COUNT_CHECK.condition_logic: len(pipeline.Stages[0].Deployments) <= 1 AND (deploymentLimit == null OR all(s in pipeline.Stages[1:], len(s.Deployments) <= deploymentLimit))
CODEPIPELINE_DEPLOYMENT_COUNT_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the first deployment stage of AWS CodePipeline performs more than one deployment. Optionally checks if each of the subsequent remaining stages deploy to more than the specified number of deployments (deploymentLimit).
CODEPIPELINE_DEPLOYMENT_COUNT_CHECK.remediation_summary: Restructure the pipeline so the first deployment stage targets a single environment, splitting fan-out across additional stages with an action count below deploymentLimit. Use aws codepipeline update-pipeline or Terraform aws_codepipeline.stage.action to refactor, and require manual approval before broad deployments.
CODEPIPELINE_DEPLOYMENT_COUNT_CHECK.title: CodePipeline first deployment stage must deploy to only one environment

CW_LOGGROUP_RETENTION_PERIOD_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any CloudWatch Logs log group (optionally only those whose name matches LogGroupNames prefixes) whose RetentionInDays is below MinRetentionTime (default 365). Log groups set to 'never expire' are compliant.
CW_LOGGROUP_RETENTION_PERIOD_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon CloudWatch LogGroup retention period is set to greater than 365 days or else a specified retention period. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the retention period is less than MinRetentionTime, if specified, or else 365 days.
CW_LOGGROUP_RETENTION_PERIOD_CHECK.remediation_summary: Set retention on each CloudWatch log group to at least MinRetentionTime via aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name <name> --retention-in-days 365, or Terraform aws_cloudwatch_log_group.retention_in_days = 365. Standardize via a Lambda + Config remediation that audits all log groups daily.
CW_LOGGROUP_RETENTION_PERIOD_CHECK.title: CloudWatch log groups must have a retention period set

DAX_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any DAX cluster whose SSEDescription.Status is not ENABLED.
DAX_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) clusters are encrypted. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a DAX cluster is not encrypted.
DAX_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Recreate each DAX cluster with SSESpecification.Enabled = true (DAX does not support enabling encryption in place) via aws dax create-cluster --sse-specification Enabled=true, or Terraform aws_dax_cluster.server_side_encryption { enabled = true }. Migrate clients to the new endpoint after the new cluster is healthy.
DAX_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.title: DAX clusters must be encrypted at rest

DAX_TLS_ENDPOINT_ENCRYPTION.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any DAX cluster whose ClusterEndpointEncryptionType is not TLS.
DAX_TLS_ENDPOINT_ENCRYPTION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster has ClusterEndpointEncryptionType set to TLS. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a DAX cluster is not encrypted by transport layer security (TLS).
DAX_TLS_ENDPOINT_ENCRYPTION.remediation_summary: Create new DAX clusters with ClusterEndpointEncryptionType = TLS (this cannot be changed in place) via aws dax create-cluster --cluster-endpoint-encryption-type TLS, or Terraform aws_dax_cluster.cluster_endpoint_encryption_type = "TLS". Update applications to use the TLS-enabled endpoint and a DAX client that supports TLS.
DAX_TLS_ENDPOINT_ENCRYPTION.title: DAX clusters must use TLS for endpoint encryption

DB_INSTANCE_BACKUP_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB instance whose BackupRetentionPeriod is 0 (or below backupRetentionMinimum), and optionally checks the backup window and read replica coverage.
DB_INSTANCE_BACKUP_ENABLED.condition_logic: db_instance.BackupRetentionPeriod >= COALESCE(backupRetentionMinimum, 1) AND (preferredBackupWindow == null OR db_instance.PreferredBackupWindow == preferredBackupWindow) AND (checkReadReplicas != true OR db_instance.read_replicas.all(BackupRetentionPeriod >= 1))
DB_INSTANCE_BACKUP_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if RDS DB instances have backups enabled. Optionally, the rule checks the backup retention period and the backup window.
DB_INSTANCE_BACKUP_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Set BackupRetentionPeriod to at least 1 day (typically 7-35) on the RDS DB instance and configure a preferred backup window. Use aws rds modify-db-instance --backup-retention-period or Terraform aws_db_instance.backup_retention_period and backup_window to enable automated backups.
DB_INSTANCE_BACKUP_ENABLED.title: RDS DB instances must have automated backups enabled

DMS_ENDPOINT_SSL_CONFIGURED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any AWS DMS endpoint whose SslMode is none, indicating no SSL/TLS connection to the source or target database.
DMS_ENDPOINT_SSL_CONFIGURED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) endpoints are configured with an SSL connection. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if AWS DMS does not have an SSL connection configured.
DMS_ENDPOINT_SSL_CONFIGURED.remediation_summary: Recreate each DMS endpoint with --ssl-mode set to require, verify-ca, or verify-full and supply the appropriate certificate ARN: aws dms create-endpoint --ssl-mode verify-full --certificate-arn <arn>, or Terraform aws_dms_endpoint.ssl_mode = "verify-full" with certificate_arn. Import the source DB CA via aws dms import-certificate.
DMS_ENDPOINT_SSL_CONFIGURED.title: DMS endpoints must use an SSL connection

DMS_REDIS_TLS_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any AWS DMS Redis endpoint whose SslSecurityProtocol is not ssl-encryption (TLS disabled).
DMS_REDIS_TLS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) endpoints for Redis data stores are enabled for TLS/SSL encryption of data communicated with other endpoints. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if TLS/SSL encryption is not enabled.
DMS_REDIS_TLS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Recreate any DMS Redis endpoint setting RedisSettings.SslSecurityProtocol = ssl-encryption and supplying SslCaCertificateArn. Use aws dms create-endpoint --engine-name redis --redis-settings SslSecurityProtocol=ssl-encryption,SslCaCertificateArn=<arn>, or Terraform aws_dms_endpoint.redis_settings { ssl_security_protocol = "ssl-encryption" ssl_ca_certificate_arn = ... }.
DMS_REDIS_TLS_ENABLED.title: DMS Redis endpoints must have TLS enabled

DMS_REPLICATION_NOT_PUBLIC.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any AWS DMS replication instance whose PubliclyAccessible field is true.
DMS_REPLICATION_NOT_PUBLIC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instances are public. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if PubliclyAccessible field is set to true.
DMS_REPLICATION_NOT_PUBLIC.remediation_summary: Recreate the DMS replication instance with --no-publicly-accessible (publiclyAccessible cannot be modified after create): aws dms create-replication-instance --no-publicly-accessible, or Terraform aws_dms_replication_instance.publicly_accessible = false. Use VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or VPN for cross-account migrations rather than a public IP.
DMS_REPLICATION_NOT_PUBLIC.title: DMS replication instances must not be publicly accessible

DOCDB_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any DocumentDB cluster whose StorageEncrypted is false, and optionally fails clusters whose KmsKeyId is not in kmsKeyArns.
DOCDB_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.condition_logic: docdb.Cluster.StorageEncrypted == true AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR docdb.Cluster.KmsKeyId IN kmsKeyArns)
DOCDB_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if storage encryption is enabled for your Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) clusters. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if storage encryption is not enabled.
DOCDB_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Encryption cannot be enabled on an existing DocumentDB cluster. Create a new cluster with --storage-encrypted and --kms-key-id, restore from a snapshot, switch application connection strings to the new cluster, then delete the unencrypted source. Use aws docdb create-db-cluster --storage-encrypted --kms-key-id <arn>, or Terraform aws_docdb_cluster.storage_encrypted = true with kms_key_id.
DOCDB_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.title: DocumentDB clusters must have storage encryption enabled

DOCDB_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any DocumentDB manual cluster snapshot whose AttributeValues for restore include 'all' (i.e., publicly restorable).
DOCDB_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon DocumentDB manual cluster snapshots are public. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any Amazon DocumentDB manual cluster snapshots are public.
DOCDB_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Remove 'all' from the restore attribute on any public DocumentDB manual snapshot using aws docdb modify-db-cluster-snapshot-attribute --db-cluster-snapshot-identifier <id> --attribute-name restore --values-to-remove all, or Terraform aws_docdb_cluster_snapshot with no public sharing. Share specific account IDs only when required.
DOCDB_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.title: DocumentDB manual cluster snapshots must not be public

DYNAMODB_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any DynamoDB table or global secondary index using PROVISIONED capacity without Application Auto Scaling configured for both read and write capacity (or that does not match supplied min/max/target parameters). On-demand tables are compliant.
DYNAMODB_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED.condition_logic: dynamodb.Table.BillingMode == 'PAY_PER_REQUEST' OR (exists(applicationautoscaling.ScalableTarget for table.read) AND exists(applicationautoscaling.ScalableTarget for table.write))
DYNAMODB_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon DynamoDB tables or global secondary indexes can process read/write capacity using on-demand mode or provisioned mode with auto scaling enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if either mode is used without auto scaling enabled.
DYNAMODB_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Either switch the table to on-demand (PAY_PER_REQUEST) via aws dynamodb update-table --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST, or register read/write Application Auto Scaling targets and policies (aws application-autoscaling register-scalable-target / put-scaling-policy) using the supplied min/max/target percentages. Terraform: aws_dynamodb_table.billing_mode = "PAY_PER_REQUEST" or aws_appautoscaling_target + aws_appautoscaling_policy.
DYNAMODB_AUTOSCALING_ENABLED.title: DynamoDB tables must use on-demand or auto-scaled provisioned capacity

DYNAMODB_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any DynamoDB table that is not the target of an active AWS Backup plan resource selection.
DYNAMODB_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon DynamoDB table is present in AWS Backup plans. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if DynamoDB tables are not present in any AWS Backup plan.
DYNAMODB_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the DynamoDB table to an AWS Backup plan via tag-based or ARN-based resource selection. Use aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection with the table ARN to ensure scheduled backups are created.
DYNAMODB_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.title: DynamoDB tables must be included in an AWS Backup plan

DYNAMODB_PITR_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a DynamoDB table whose ContinuousBackups/PointInTimeRecoveryDescription status is not ENABLED.
DYNAMODB_PITR_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if point-in-time recovery (PITR) is enabled for Amazon DynamoDB tables. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if PITR is not enabled for DynamoDB tables.
DYNAMODB_PITR_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable point-in-time recovery on each DynamoDB table using aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true or Terraform aws_dynamodb_table.point_in_time_recovery.enabled = true.
DYNAMODB_PITR_ENABLED.title: DynamoDB tables must have point-in-time recovery enabled

DYNAMODB_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_P.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any DynamoDB table not covered by an active AWS Backup plan, optionally filtered by tags or resourceId, with checks for vault lock retention and cross-region/account copies.
DYNAMODB_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_P.condition_logic: dynamodb_table IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
DYNAMODB_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_P.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon DynamoDB tables are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the DynamoDB Table is not covered by a backup plan.
DYNAMODB_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_P.remediation_summary: Add the DynamoDB table to an AWS Backup plan via aws backup create-backup-selection (resource ARN or tag-based selection), or Terraform aws_backup_selection.resources = [aws_dynamodb_table.app.arn]. When backupVaultLockCheck = True, store recovery points in a Backup Vault Lock with retention between minRetentionDays and maxRetentionDays.
DYNAMODB_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_P.title: DynamoDB tables must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTED_KMS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any DynamoDB table whose SSEDescription is not enabled with a KMS key, or whose KMS key ARN is not in kmsKeyArns.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTED_KMS.condition_logic: dynamodb.Table.SSEDescription.Status == 'ENABLED' AND dynamodb.Table.SSEDescription.SSEType == 'KMS' AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR dynamodb.Table.SSEDescription.KMSMasterKeyArn IN kmsKeyArns)
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTED_KMS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon DynamoDB table is encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (KMS). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Amazon DynamoDB table is not encrypted with AWS KMS. The rule is also NON_COMPLIANT if the encrypted AWS KMS key is not present in kmsKeyArns input parameter.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTED_KMS.remediation_summary: Enable KMS encryption with an approved CMK on each DynamoDB table via aws dynamodb update-table --sse-specification Enabled=true,SSEType=KMS,KMSMasterKeyId=<arn>, or Terraform aws_dynamodb_table.server_side_encryption { enabled = true kms_key_arn = ... }. Restrict KMS key ARN to those in kmsKeyArns.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTED_KMS.title: DynamoDB tables must be encrypted with AWS KMS

DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any DynamoDB table whose SSEDescription.Status is not ENABLED or ENABLING.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Amazon DynamoDB tables are encrypted and checks their status. The rule is COMPLIANT if the status is enabled or enabling.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Turn on server-side encryption for each DynamoDB table via aws dynamodb update-table --sse-specification Enabled=true,SSEType=KMS, or Terraform aws_dynamodb_table.server_side_encryption.enabled = true. New tables created via the console default to encrypted.
DYNAMODB_TABLE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.title: DynamoDB tables must have server-side encryption enabled

DYNAMODB_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account when total provisioned read or write capacity exceeds accountRCUThresholdPercentage / accountWCUThresholdPercentage of the account-level service limits (default 80% each).
DYNAMODB_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if provisioned DynamoDB throughput is approaching the maximum limit for your account. By default, the rule checks if provisioned throughput exceeds a threshold of 80 percent of your account limits.
DYNAMODB_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT_CHECK.remediation_summary: Reduce provisioned throughput by switching tables to on-demand (PAY_PER_REQUEST) where workloads are spiky, or request a Service Quotas increase via aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code dynamodb. Track provisioned vs. limit with CloudWatch alarms on AccountProvisionedReadCapacityUtilization / AccountProvisionedWriteCapacityUtilization.
DYNAMODB_THROUGHPUT_LIMIT_CHECK.title: Account-level DynamoDB provisioned throughput must stay below limits

EBS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EBS volume not covered by an AWS Backup plan resource selection.
EBS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Check if Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes are added in backup plans of AWS Backup. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Amazon EBS volumes are not included in backup plans.
EBS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Include the EBS volume in an AWS Backup plan using a tag-based or ARN-based selection. Apply via aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection so the volume is regularly snapshotted into a backup vault.
EBS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.title: EBS volumes must be included in an AWS Backup plan

EBS_OPTIMIZED_INSTANCE.condition_description: Checks if Amazon EBS optimization is enabled for your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances that can be Amazon EBS-optimized. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if EBS optimization is not enabled for an Amazon EC2 instance that can be EBS-optimized. Note EC2 instances which are EBS-optimized by default always result in rule evaluations returning COMPLIANT. Identifier: EBS_OPTIMIZED_INSTANCE Resource Types: AWS::EC2::Instance Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Mexico

The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if EBS optimization is not enabled for an Amazon EC2 instance that can be EBS-optimized. Note EC2 instances which are EBS-optimized by default always result in rule evaluations returning COMPLIANT. EBS_OPTIMIZED_INSTANCE.title: Ebs Optimized Instance

EBS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EBS volume not covered by an active AWS Backup plan, optionally filtered by tags or resourceId, with optional vault lock retention and cross-region/account copy checks.
EBS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: ebs_volume IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
EBS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon EBS volume is not covered by a backup plan.
EBS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add EBS volumes to an AWS Backup plan via aws backup create-backup-selection (tag-based or ARN-based) or Terraform aws_backup_selection.resources = [aws_ebs_volume.app.arn]. When backupVaultLockCheck = True, store recovery points in a Backup Vault Lock with retention between minRetentionDays and maxRetentionDays.
EBS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: EBS volumes must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

EBS_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_RESTORABLE_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EBS snapshot whose RestorableByUserIds includes 'all' (i.e., publicly restorable).
EBS_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_RESTORABLE_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots are not publicly restorable. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if one or more individual snapshots with RestorableByUserIds field are set to all.
EBS_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_RESTORABLE_CHECK.remediation_summary: Remove the public createVolumePermission from each EBS snapshot via aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id <id> --create-volume-permission '{"Remove":[{"Group":"all"}]}', or Terraform aws_ebs_snapshot with no public sharing. Share with specific account IDs only when needed.
EBS_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_RESTORABLE_CHECK.title: EBS snapshots must not be publicly restorable

EC2_CLIENT_VPN_NOT_AUTHORIZE_ALL.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any AWS Client VPN endpoint whose authorization rules contain AccessAll = true (i.e., grants access to every connected client).
EC2_CLIENT_VPN_NOT_AUTHORIZE_ALL.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the AWS Client VPN authorization rules authorizes connection access for all clients. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'AccessAll' is present and set to true.
EC2_CLIENT_VPN_NOT_AUTHORIZE_ALL.remediation_summary: Replace AccessAll = true authorization rules on each Client VPN endpoint with rules scoped to specific Active Directory groups via aws ec2 revoke-client-vpn-ingress / authorize-client-vpn-ingress --access-group-id <id>, or Terraform aws_ec2_client_vpn_authorization_rule.access_group_id. Avoid authorize-all-groups true.
EC2_CLIENT_VPN_NOT_AUTHORIZE_ALL.title: Client VPN endpoints must not authorize access for all clients

EC2_EBS_ENCRYPTION_BY_DEFAULT.condition_description: Periodic account-level rule that calls EC2 GetEbsEncryptionByDefault and fails the region if the account-level EBS-encryption-by-default flag is disabled.
EC2_EBS_ENCRYPTION_BY_DEFAULT.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption is enabled by default. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the encryption is not enabled.
EC2_EBS_ENCRYPTION_BY_DEFAULT.remediation_summary: Enable EBS encryption by default in every Region using aws ec2 enable-ebs-encryption-by-default (or the EC2 console > EBS Encryption setting). Optionally configure a default KMS key with aws ec2 modify-ebs-default-kms-key-id, or set this in Terraform via the aws_ebs_encryption_by_default and aws_ebs_default_kms_key resources.
EC2_EBS_ENCRYPTION_BY_DEFAULT.title: EBS encryption by default must be enabled at the account level

EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that inspects each EC2 instance's MetadataOptions and fails the instance if HttpTokens is set to optional (IMDSv1 allowed). HttpTokens must be required to enforce IMDSv2.
EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether your Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance metadata version is configured with Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the HttpTokens is set to optional.
EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK.remediation_summary: Force IMDSv2 on each EC2 instance by setting HttpTokens to required. Use aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --http-tokens required (and --http-endpoint enabled) or Terraform aws_instance.metadata_options { http_tokens = "required", http_endpoint = "enabled" }; bake into launch templates / AMIs for new instances.
EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK.title: EC2 instances must require IMDSv2

EC2_INSTANCES_IN_VPC.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 instance with no VpcId, or whose VpcId does not match the optional vpcId parameter. The Config rule identifier is INSTANCES_IN_VPC.
EC2_INSTANCES_IN_VPC.condition_logic: ec2_instance.VpcId != null AND (vpcId == null OR ec2_instance.VpcId == vpcId)
EC2_INSTANCES_IN_VPC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your EC2 instances belong to a virtual private cloud (VPC). Optionally, you can specify the VPC ID to associate with your instances.
EC2_INSTANCES_IN_VPC.remediation_summary: Migrate any EC2-Classic instances or instances launched outside the approved VPC to a VPC subnet by stopping, snapshotting, and re-launching with --subnet-id (and the desired vpcId). Block EC2-Classic at the account level via aws ec2 enable-vpc-classic-link-dns-support and IAM SCPs that require ec2:Subnet on RunInstances.
EC2_INSTANCES_IN_VPC.title: EC2 instances must run in a VPC

EC2_INSTANCE_DETAILED_MONITORING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 instance whose Monitoring.State is not enabled (i.e., default 5-minute monitoring instead of 1-minute detailed monitoring).
EC2_INSTANCE_DETAILED_MONITORING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if detailed monitoring is enabled for EC2 instances. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if detailed monitoring is not enabled.
EC2_INSTANCE_DETAILED_MONITORING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable detailed (1-minute) monitoring on each EC2 instance via aws ec2 monitor-instances --instance-ids <id>, or Terraform aws_instance.monitoring = true. Bake into launch templates / Auto Scaling launch configurations so new instances inherit the setting.
EC2_INSTANCE_DETAILED_MONITORING_ENABLED.title: EC2 instances must have detailed monitoring enabled

EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI.condition_description: Checks if running or stopped EC2 instances were launched with Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) that meet your Allowed AMIs criteria. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an AMI doesn't meet the Allowed AMIs criteria and the Allowed AMIs settings isn't disabled. Valid values are "running" and "stopped".
EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI.framework_control_requirement: Checks if running or stopped EC2 instances were launched with Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) that meet your Allowed AMIs criteria. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an AMI doesn't meet the Allowed AMIs criteria and the Allowed AMIs settings isn't disabled. Identifier: EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI Resource Types: AWS::EC2::Instance Trigger type: Configuration changes and Periodic AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: InstanceStateNameList (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separate list of Amazon EC2 instance states for the rule to check. Valid values are "running" and "stopped".
EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHED_WITH_ALLOWED_AMI.title: Ec2 Instance Launched With Allowed Ami

EC2_INSTANCE_MANAGED_BY_SYSTEMS_MANAGER.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any running EC2 instance not visible in SSM ManagedInstanceInventory (SSM agent stopped or terminated). Stopped instances are out of scope. The Config identifier is EC2_INSTANCE_MANAGED_BY_SSM.
EC2_INSTANCE_MANAGED_BY_SYSTEMS_MANAGER.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon EC2 instances are managed by AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an EC2 instance is running and the SSM Agent is stopped, or if an EC2 instance is running and the SSM Agent is terminated.
EC2_INSTANCE_MANAGED_BY_SYSTEMS_MANAGER.remediation_summary: Attach an instance profile that grants AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, install/restart the SSM Agent (sudo systemctl enable --now amazon-ssm-agent), and ensure the VPC has reachability to ssm/ec2messages/ssmmessages endpoints (PrivateLink or NAT). Terraform: aws_instance.iam_instance_profile attached to a role with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.
EC2_INSTANCE_MANAGED_BY_SYSTEMS_MANAGER.title: EC2 instances must be managed by AWS Systems Manager

EC2_INSTANCE_MULTIPLE_ENI_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) uses multiple Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) or Elastic Fabric Adapters (EFAs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT an Amazon EC2 instance use multiple network interfaces. Identifier: EC2_INSTANCE_MULTIPLE_ENI_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::EC2::Instance Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: NetworkInterfaceIds (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of network instance IDs
EC2_INSTANCE_MULTIPLE_ENI_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) uses multiple Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) or Elastic Fabric Adapters (EFAs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT an Amazon EC2 instance use multiple network interfaces. Identifier: EC2_INSTANCE_MULTIPLE_ENI_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::EC2::Instance Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: NetworkInterfaceIds (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of network instance IDs

EC2_INSTANCE_MULTIPLE_ENI_CHECK.title: Ec2 Instance Multiple Eni Check

EC2_INSTANCE_NO_PUBLIC_IP.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 instance whose configuration item contains a publicIp field (IPv4 only).
EC2_INSTANCE_NO_PUBLIC_IP.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances have a public IP association. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the publicIp field is present in the Amazon EC2 instance configuration item. This rule applies only to IPv4.
EC2_INSTANCE_NO_PUBLIC_IP.remediation_summary: Move EC2 workloads into private subnets and route egress through a NAT gateway, dropping the public IP. Detach Elastic IPs (aws ec2 disassociate-address) and disable subnet AssignPublicIpOnLaunch (aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --no-map-public-ip-on-launch). Use a load balancer or AWS Verified Access for inbound public access.
EC2_INSTANCE_NO_PUBLIC_IP.title: EC2 instances must not have public IPv4 addresses

EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE_ATTACHED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 instance with no IamInstanceProfile attached, or whose attached profile ARN is not in the optional IamInstanceProfileArnList allow list.
EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE_ATTACHED.condition_logic: ec2_instance.IamInstanceProfile.Arn != null AND (IamInstanceProfileArnList == null OR ec2_instance.IamInstanceProfile.Arn IN IamInstanceProfileArnList)
EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE_ATTACHED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an EC2 instance has an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) profile attached to it. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if no IAM profile is attached to the EC2 instance.
EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE_ATTACHED.remediation_summary: Attach an IAM instance profile to each EC2 instance via aws ec2 associate-iam-instance-profile or Terraform aws_instance.iam_instance_profile / aws_iam_instance_profile, granting the instance only the permissions it needs and removing any embedded long-lived credentials.
EC2_INSTANCE_PROFILE_ATTACHED.title: EC2 instances must have an IAM instance profile attached

EC2_LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 launch template whose default version has at least one NetworkInterface with AssociatePublicIpAddress = true, unless the template ID appears in exemptedLaunchTemplates.
EC2_LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.condition_logic: all(ni in launchTemplate.DefaultVersion.NetworkInterfaces, ni.AssociatePublicIpAddress == false) OR launchTemplate.LaunchTemplateId IN exemptedLaunchTemplates
EC2_LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon EC2 Launch Templates are set to assign public IP addresses to Network Interfaces. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the default version of an EC2 Launch Template has at least 1 Network Interface with 'AssociatePublicIpAddress' set to 'true'.
EC2_LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.remediation_summary: Create a new launch-template version with NetworkInterfaces[*].AssociatePublicIpAddress = false (or remove the override entirely) via aws ec2 create-launch-template-version, then set it as default. Terraform: aws_launch_template.network_interfaces { associate_public_ip_address = false } and update aws_launch_template.default_version.
EC2_LAUNCH_TEMPLATE_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.title: EC2 launch templates must not assign public IPs

EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_ASSOCIATION_COMPLIAN.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any AWS Systems Manager association compliance item whose Status is not COMPLIANT.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_ASSOCIATION_COMPLIAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the status of the AWS Systems Manager association compliance is COMPLIANT or NON_COMPLIANT after the association execution on the instance. The rule is compliant if the field status is COMPLIANT.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_ASSOCIATION_COMPLIAN.remediation_summary: Investigate failing associations in the Systems Manager State Manager console (or aws ssm describe-association-execution-targets) and remediate the underlying configuration drift. Re-run associations with aws ssm start-associations-once. Use Terraform aws_ssm_association to ensure documents are versioned and parameters consistent.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_ASSOCIATION_COMPLIAN.title: AWS Systems Manager associations must report compliant

EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STA.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any AWS Systems Manager patch compliance item whose Status is not COMPLIANT.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STA.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the compliance status of the AWS Systems Manager patch compliance is COMPLIANT or NON_COMPLIANT after the patch installation on the instance. The rule is compliant if the field status is COMPLIANT.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STA.remediation_summary: Apply missing patches to instances reported NON_COMPLIANT using AWS-RunPatchBaseline via aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunPatchBaseline --parameters '{"Operation":["Install"]}', or by attaching the instances to a maintenance window. Define a baseline with aws ssm create-patch-baseline / Terraform aws_ssm_patch_baseline + aws_ssm_patch_group.
EC2_MANAGEDINSTANCE_PATCH_COMPLIANCE_STA.title: AWS Systems Manager patch compliance must be COMPLIANT

EC2_NO_AMAZON_KEY_PAIR.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any running EC2 instance launched with a KeyName (i.e., uses an Amazon key pair).
EC2_NO_AMAZON_KEY_PAIR.framework_control_requirement: Checks if running Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances are launched using amazon key pairs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a running EC2 instance is launched with a key pair.
EC2_NO_AMAZON_KEY_PAIR.remediation_summary: Stop using SSH key pairs for new instances; relaunch instances without --key-name and rely on AWS Systems Manager Session Manager / EC2 Instance Connect for shell access. Terraform: omit aws_instance.key_name or aws_launch_template.key_name, and ensure SSM agent + IAM role are configured.
EC2_NO_AMAZON_KEY_PAIR.title: EC2 instances must not be launched with an Amazon key pair

EC2_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any running EC2 instance not covered by an AWS Backup plan, optionally enforcing tag/resourceId filters and a locked Backup Vault with retention within minRetentionDays/maxRetentionDays.
EC2_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: ec2_instance.State == 'running' AND ec2_instance.arn IN aws_backup_plan.selections.resources AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
EC2_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon EC2 instance is not covered by a backup plan.
EC2_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Cover each running EC2 instance with an AWS Backup plan via tag- or ARN-based selection (aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection). Where required, target a locked Backup Vault and configure cross-Region/cross-account copy actions to satisfy retention guarantees.
EC2_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: EC2 instances must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIO.condition_description: Checks if non-default security groups are attached to Elastic network interfaces (ENIs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the security group is not associated with an ENI. Security groups not owned by the calling account evaluate as NOT_APPLICABLE. Note This rule reports on the AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup resource type. However, in order for the rule to run effectively, you must enable the recording of the AWS::EC2::NetworkInterface resource type. Identifier: EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIODIC Resource Types: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup Trigger type: Periodic AWS Region: All supported AWS regions
EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIO.framework_control_requirement: Checks if non-default security groups are attached to Elastic network interfaces (ENIs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the security group is not associated with an ENI. Security groups not owned by the calling account evaluate as NOT_APPLICABLE. Note This rule reports on the AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup resource type. However, in order for the rule to run effectively, you must enable the recording of the AWS::EC2::NetworkInterface resource type. Identifier: EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIODIC Resource Types: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup Trigger type: Periodic AWS Region: All supported AWS regions
EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIO.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIODIC. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
EC2_SECURITY_GROUP_ATTACHED_TO_ENI_PERIO.title: Ec2 Security Group Attached To Eni Periodic

EC2_STOPPED_INSTANCE.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EC2 instance that has been in the stopped state for more than AllowedDays (default 30 days). Instances whose stopped duration cannot be determined are also non-compliant.
EC2_STOPPED_INSTANCE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if there are Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instances stopped for more than the allowed number of days. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the state of an Amazon EC2 instance has been stopped for longer than the allowed number of days, or if the amount of time cannot be determined.
EC2_STOPPED_INSTANCE.remediation_summary: Decide whether to terminate (aws ec2 terminate-instances) or restart stopped EC2 instances older than AllowedDays, after preserving any required EBS snapshots. Tag long-running stopped instances with an owner / business justification, and automate cleanup with EventBridge schedules + Systems Manager Automation.
EC2_STOPPED_INSTANCE.title: EC2 instances must not be stopped longer than the allowed period

EC2_TRANSIT_GATEWAY_AUTO_VPC_ATTACH_DISA.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EC2 Transit Gateway whose AutoAcceptSharedAttachments is set to enable.
EC2_TRANSIT_GATEWAY_AUTO_VPC_ATTACH_DISA.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Transit Gateways have 'AutoAcceptSharedAttachments' enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a Transit Gateway if 'AutoAcceptSharedAttachments' is set to 'enable'.
EC2_TRANSIT_GATEWAY_AUTO_VPC_ATTACH_DISA.remediation_summary: Set AutoAcceptSharedAttachments = disable on each Transit Gateway via aws ec2 modify-transit-gateway --transit-gateway-id <id> --options AutoAcceptSharedAttachments=disable, or Terraform aws_ec2_transit_gateway.auto_accept_shared_attachments = "disable". Manually approve each shared attachment after review.
EC2_TRANSIT_GATEWAY_AUTO_VPC_ATTACH_DISA.title: EC2 Transit Gateways must not auto-accept VPC attachments

EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EBS volume not attached to an EC2 instance, or attached to a terminated instance. Optionally fails attached volumes whose Attachment.DeleteOnTermination differs from deleteOnTermination.
EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK.condition_logic: ebs_volume.State == 'in-use' AND ebs_volume.Attachments[0].InstanceState != 'terminated' AND (deleteOnTermination == null OR ebs_volume.Attachments[0].DeleteOnTermination == deleteOnTermination)
EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if EBS volumes are attached to EC2 instances. Optionally checks if EBS volumes are marked for deletion when an instance is terminated. The rule is COMPLIANT if an EBS volume is attached to running or stopped EC2 instances. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an EBS volume is not attached to any EC2 instance or is attached to a terminated EC2 instance.
EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK.remediation_summary: Snapshot then delete unattached EBS volumes via aws ec2 create-snapshot followed by aws ec2 delete-volume, or remediate via Terraform by removing the resource. When deleteOnTermination = True is required, set Attachment.DeleteOnTermination = true (aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute) so volumes follow instance lifecycle.
EC2_VOLUME_INUSE_CHECK.title: EBS volumes must be attached to active EC2 instances

ECR_PRIVATE_IMAGE_SCANNING_ENABLED.title: Ecr Private Image Scanning Enabled

ECR_PRIVATE_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CONFIGURED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any private ECR repository that does not have a lifecycle policy configured.
ECR_PRIVATE_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CONFIGURED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a private Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) repository has at least one lifecycle policy configured. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if no lifecycle policy is configured for the ECR private repository.
ECR_PRIVATE_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CONFIGURED.remediation_summary: Attach a lifecycle policy to each private ECR repository to expire untagged or stale images via aws ecr put-lifecycle-policy --repository-name <name> --lifecycle-policy-text file://policy.json, or Terraform aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy.policy. Apply the policy organization-wide via Service Control Policies and an automation pipeline.
ECR_PRIVATE_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CONFIGURED.title: Private ECR repositories must have a lifecycle policy configured

ECS_CONTAINERS_READONLY_ACCESS.remediation_summary: Set readonlyRootFilesystem = true in every container definition via aws ecs register-task-definition (with updated container definitions JSON), or Terraform aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions JSON should include "readonlyRootFilesystem": true. Provide writable space through tmpfs or specific volumeMounts.
ECS_CONTAINERS_READONLY_ACCESS.title: ECS task containers must have a read-only root filesystem

ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOG_CONFIGURATION.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails the latest active ECS task definition revision if any container definition lacks logConfiguration or has it set to null.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOG_CONFIGURATION.condition_logic: all(c in ecs.TaskDefinition.ContainerDefinitions, c.LogConfiguration != null AND c.LogConfiguration.LogDriver != null)
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOG_CONFIGURATION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if logConfiguration is set on active ECS Task Definitions. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an active ECSTaskDefinition does not have the logConfiguration resource defined or the value for logConfiguration is null in at least one container definition.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOG_CONFIGURATION.remediation_summary: Ensure every container definition includes a logConfiguration block (e.g., awslogs driver to a CloudWatch Logs group) and re-register the task definition via aws ecs register-task-definition, or Terraform aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions with "logConfiguration": { "logDriver": "awslogs", "options": {...} }.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_LOG_CONFIGURATION.title: ECS task definitions must configure container logging
