ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_PID_MODE_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails the latest active ECS task definition revision whose pidMode is set to 'host', sharing the host PID namespace with containers.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_PID_MODE_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if ECSTaskDefinitions are configured to share a host's process namespace with its Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the pidMode parameter is set to 'host'.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_PID_MODE_CHECK.remediation_summary: Re-register the task definition without pidMode = host (omit it or set to task) via aws ecs register-task-definition, or Terraform aws_ecs_task_definition.pid_mode = "task". Refactor any tooling that depended on the host PID namespace.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_PID_MODE_CHECK.title: ECS task definitions must not share the host PID namespace

ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_USER_FOR_HOST_MODE_C.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails ECS task definitions running with networkMode = host AND privileged != true AND user (or null) == root. SkipInactiveTaskDefinitions controls whether inactive definitions are evaluated.
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_USER_FOR_HOST_MODE_C.condition_logic: ecs.TaskDefinition.NetworkMode != 'host' OR any(c in ContainerDefinitions, c.Privileged == true) OR any(c in ContainerDefinitions, c.User != null AND c.User != 'root' AND c.User != '0')
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_USER_FOR_HOST_MODE_C.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon ECS task definitions with host network mode have privileged OR nonroot in the container definition. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the latest active revision of a task definition has privileged=false (or is null) AND user=root (or is null).
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_USER_FOR_HOST_MODE_C.remediation_summary: For task definitions using networkMode = host, either drop host networking, or set container user to a non-root UID/name (and avoid privileged = true unless explicitly required). Re-register via aws ecs register-task-definition, or update Terraform aws_ecs_task_definition.container_definitions with "user": "1000".
ECS_TASK_DEFINITION_USER_FOR_HOST_MODE_C.title: Host-mode ECS tasks must run as non-root or be privileged

EFS_ENCRYPTED_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EFS file system with Encrypted = false, or whose KmsKeyId does not match the optional KmsKeyId parameter.
EFS_ENCRYPTED_CHECK.condition_logic: efs.FileSystem.Encrypted == true AND (KmsKeyId == null OR efs.FileSystem.KmsKeyId == KmsKeyId)
EFS_ENCRYPTED_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is configured to encrypt the file data using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the encrypted key is set to false on DescribeFileSystems or if the KmsKeyId key on DescribeFileSystems does not match the KmsKeyId parameter.
EFS_ENCRYPTED_CHECK.remediation_summary: EFS encryption cannot be enabled in place. Create a new file system with --encrypted (and the required --kms-key-id), copy data with AWS DataSync or rsync, repoint mount targets, then delete the original. Use aws efs create-file-system --encrypted --kms-key-id <arn>, or Terraform aws_efs_file_system.encrypted = true and kms_key_id.
EFS_ENCRYPTED_CHECK.title: EFS file systems must be encrypted with AWS KMS

EFS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EFS file system that is not selected for backup by any active AWS Backup plan.
EFS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file systems are added in the backup plans of AWS Backup. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if EFS file systems are not included in the backup plans.
EFS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the EFS file system to an AWS Backup plan using tag-based or ARN-based resource selection (aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection) so its file system is automatically backed up to a Backup Vault.
EFS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.title: EFS file systems must be included in an AWS Backup plan

EFS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EFS file system not covered by an active AWS Backup plan, optionally filtered by tags or resourceId, with optional vault lock and cross-region/account checks.
EFS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: efs_filesystem IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
EFS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the EFS File System is not covered by a backup plan.
EFS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add EFS file systems to an AWS Backup plan via aws backup create-backup-selection (tag- or ARN-based) or Terraform aws_backup_selection.resources = [aws_efs_file_system.app.arn]. When backupVaultLockCheck = True, store recovery points in a Backup Vault Lock with retention between minRetentionDays and maxRetentionDays.
EFS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: EFS file systems must be protected by an AWS Backup plan
