EKS_CLUSTER_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EKS cluster whose Logging.ClusterLogging does not have all five log types (api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler) enabled.
EKS_CLUSTER_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster is configured with logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if logging for Amazon EKS clusters is not enabled for all log types.
EKS_CLUSTER_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable all control-plane log types on each EKS cluster via aws eks update-cluster-config --name <cluster> --logging '{"clusterLogging":[{"types":["api","audit","authenticator","controllerManager","scheduler"],"enabled":true}]}', or Terraform aws_eks_cluster.enabled_cluster_log_types = ["api","audit","authenticator","controllerManager","scheduler"].
EKS_CLUSTER_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: EKS clusters must enable control-plane logging for all types

EKS_CLUSTER_OLDEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any EKS cluster running the Kubernetes version specified in oldestVersionSupported, indicating it is at end-of-support and should be upgraded.
EKS_CLUSTER_OLDEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster is running the oldest supported version. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an EKS cluster is running oldest supported version (equal to the parameter 'oldestVersionSupported').
EKS_CLUSTER_OLDEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION.remediation_summary: Plan and execute a Kubernetes version upgrade on each affected EKS cluster via aws eks update-cluster-version --name <cluster> --kubernetes-version <next-version>, then upgrade managed node groups (aws eks update-nodegroup-version) and add-ons. Use Terraform aws_eks_cluster.version, aws_eks_node_group.version, and aws_eks_addon.addon_version, after testing in non-production.
EKS_CLUSTER_OLDEST_SUPPORTED_VERSION.title: EKS clusters must not run the oldest supported Kubernetes version

EKS_CLUSTER_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EKS cluster whose EncryptionConfig is missing or whose Resources do not include 'secrets', and optionally fails clusters whose KMS key ARN is not in kmsKeyArns.
EKS_CLUSTER_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.condition_logic: exists(cfg in eks.Cluster.EncryptionConfig WHERE 'secrets' IN cfg.Resources) AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR cfg.Provider.KeyArn IN kmsKeyArns)
EKS_CLUSTER_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon EKS clusters are configured to have Kubernetes secrets encrypted using AWS KMS. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an EKS cluster does not have an encryptionConfig resource or if encryptionConfig does not name secrets as a resource.
EKS_CLUSTER_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Configure envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets via aws eks associate-encryption-config --cluster-name <cluster> --encryption-config 'resources=[secrets],provider={keyArn=<kms-arn>}', or Terraform aws_eks_cluster.encryption_config { resources = ["secrets"] provider { key_arn = ... } }. Use a KMS key ARN listed in kmsKeyArns.
EKS_CLUSTER_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.title: EKS clusters must encrypt Kubernetes secrets with KMS

EKS_ENDPOINT_NO_PUBLIC_ACCESS.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EKS cluster whose ResourcesVpcConfig.EndpointPublicAccess is true.
EKS_ENDPOINT_NO_PUBLIC_ACCESS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) endpoint is not publicly accessible. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the endpoint is publicly accessible.
EKS_ENDPOINT_NO_PUBLIC_ACCESS.remediation_summary: Disable the EKS public endpoint and rely on the private endpoint via aws eks update-cluster-config --name <cluster> --resources-vpc-config endpointPublicAccess=false,endpointPrivateAccess=true, or Terraform aws_eks_cluster.vpc_config { endpoint_public_access = false endpoint_private_access = true }. Reach the API via VPN, Direct Connect, or a bastion in the same VPC.
EKS_ENDPOINT_NO_PUBLIC_ACCESS.title: EKS cluster endpoints must not be publicly accessible

EKS_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EKS cluster lacking an encryptionConfig that names secrets, or whose KMS key does not match the optional kmsKeyArns parameter.
EKS_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.condition_logic: exists(cfg in eks.Cluster.EncryptionConfig WHERE 'secrets' IN cfg.Resources) AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR cfg.Provider.KeyArn IN kmsKeyArns)
EKS_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service clusters are configured to have Kubernetes secrets encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys.
EKS_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Associate envelope encryption on the EKS cluster via aws eks associate-encryption-config --cluster-name <cluster> --encryption-config 'resources=[secrets],provider={keyArn=<arn>}', or Terraform aws_eks_cluster.encryption_config { resources = ["secrets"] provider { key_arn = ... } }. Pin the KMS key to one in kmsKeyArns when configured.
EKS_SECRETS_ENCRYPTED.title: EKS clusters must encrypt secrets with a KMS key

ELASTICACHE_REDIS_CLUSTER_AUTOMATIC_BACK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails an ElastiCache Redis cluster or replication group whose SnapshotRetentionLimit is less than the snapshotRetentionPeriod parameter (default 15 days).
ELASTICACHE_REDIS_CLUSTER_AUTOMATIC_BACK.framework_control_requirement: Check if the Amazon ElastiCache Redis clusters have automatic backup turned on. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the SnapshotRetentionLimit for Redis cluster is less than the SnapshotRetentionPeriod parameter. For example: If the parameter is 15 then the rule is non-compliant if the snapshotRetentionPeriod is between 0-15.
ELASTICACHE_REDIS_CLUSTER_AUTOMATIC_BACK.remediation_summary: Increase SnapshotRetentionLimit on each ElastiCache Redis cluster or replication group to at least snapshotRetentionPeriod (default 15) days. Use aws elasticache modify-cache-cluster --snapshot-retention-limit / modify-replication-group, or Terraform aws_elasticache_cluster.snapshot_retention_limit / aws_elasticache_replication_group.snapshot_retention_limit.
ELASTICACHE_REDIS_CLUSTER_AUTOMATIC_BACK.title: ElastiCache Redis clusters must have automatic backups retained for the configured period

ELASTICSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any OpenSearch / Elasticsearch domain whose EncryptionAtRestOptions.Enabled is not true.
ELASTICSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon OpenSearch Service (previously called Elasticsearch) domains have encryption at rest configuration enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the EncryptionAtRestOptions field is not enabled.
ELASTICSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.remediation_summary: Encryption at rest must be enabled at domain creation. Create a new domain with --encryption-at-rest-options Enabled=true,KmsKeyId=<arn>, snapshot the legacy domain to S3 and restore into the new domain, then delete the legacy resource. Terraform: aws_opensearch_domain.encrypt_at_rest { enabled = true kms_key_id = ... }.
ELASTICSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.title: OpenSearch domains must have encryption at rest enabled

ELASTICSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any OpenSearch / Elasticsearch domain whose endpoint is public (i.e., VPCOptions are absent).
ELASTICSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon OpenSearch Service (previously called Elasticsearch) domains are in Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an OpenSearch Service domain endpoint is public.
ELASTICSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.remediation_summary: VPC placement must be selected at domain creation. Provision a new OpenSearch domain inside private subnets (--vpc-options SubnetIds=...,SecurityGroupIds=...), migrate data via snapshots, and delete the legacy public domain. Terraform: aws_opensearch_domain.vpc_options { subnet_ids = ... security_group_ids = ... }.
ELASTICSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.title: OpenSearch domains must be deployed in a VPC

ELASTICSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any OpenSearch / Elasticsearch domain whose LogPublishingOptions does not have at least one log type enabled, or whose enabled log types do not match logTypes.
ELASTICSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_logic: any(t in opensearch.Domain.LogPublishingOptions, t.Enabled == true) AND (logTypes == null OR opensearch.Domain.LogPublishingOptions.keys() superset_of logTypes)
ELASTICSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.framework_control_requirement: Checks if OpenSearch Service (previously called Elasticsearch) domains are configured to send logs to CloudWatch Logs. The rule is COMPLIANT if a log is enabled for an OpenSearch Service domain. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if logging is not configured.
ELASTICSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.remediation_summary: Enable LogPublishingOptions for SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS, INDEX_SLOW_LOGS, ES_APPLICATION_LOGS, and AUDIT_LOGS as required, each pointing at a CloudWatch Logs log group. Use aws opensearch update-domain-config --log-publishing-options or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.log_publishing_options { ... } and grant the OpenSearch service role logs:PutLogEvents on the target log group.
ELASTICSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.title: OpenSearch domains must publish logs to CloudWatch Logs

ELASTICSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CH.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any OpenSearch / Elasticsearch domain whose NodeToNodeEncryptionOptions.Enabled is not true.
ELASTICSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CH.framework_control_requirement: Check that Amazon OpenSearch Service nodes are encrypted end to end. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the node-to-node encryption is disabled on the domain.
ELASTICSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CH.remediation_summary: Node-to-node encryption can only be enabled at domain creation. Create a new OpenSearch domain with --node-to-node-encryption-options Enabled=true, migrate via snapshots, then delete the legacy domain. Terraform: aws_opensearch_domain.node_to_node_encryption { enabled = true }.
ELASTICSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CH.title: OpenSearch domains must enable node-to-node encryption

ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Elastic Beanstalk environment whose option StreamLogs is false, optionally also failing if RetentionInDays or DeleteOnTerminate do not match parameters.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_logic: elasticbeanstalk.Environment.OptionSettings['aws:elasticbeanstalk:cloudwatch:logs'].StreamLogs == 'true' AND (RetentionInDays == null OR Setting['logs:RetentionInDays'] == RetentionInDays) AND (DeleteOnTerminate == null OR Setting['logs:DeleteOnTerminate'] == DeleteOnTerminate)
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments are configured to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the value of StreamLogs is false.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.remediation_summary: Enable CloudWatch Logs streaming on each Elastic Beanstalk environment by setting aws:elasticbeanstalk:cloudwatch:logs StreamLogs = true (and RetentionInDays / DeleteOnTerminate as required) via aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment --option-settings, or Terraform aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.setting { namespace = "aws:elasticbeanstalk:cloudwatch:logs" name = "StreamLogs" value = "true" }.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.title: Elastic Beanstalk environments must stream logs to CloudWatch

ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_MANAGED_UPDATES_ENABLE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Elastic Beanstalk environment whose ManagedActionsEnabled is not true, or whose UpdateLevel does not match the optional UpdateLevel parameter.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_MANAGED_UPDATES_ENABLE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if managed platform updates in an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment is enabled. The rule is COMPLIANT if the value for ManagedActionsEnabled is set to true. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the value for ManagedActionsEnabled is set to false, or if a parameter is provided and its value does not match the existing configurations.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_MANAGED_UPDATES_ENABLE.remediation_summary: Turn on managed platform updates on each Elastic Beanstalk environment by setting aws:elasticbeanstalk:managedactions ManagedActionsEnabled = true (PreferredStartTime, ServiceRoleForManagedUpdates) and aws:elasticbeanstalk:managedactions:platformupdate UpdateLevel = patch or minor via aws elasticbeanstalk update-environment, or Terraform aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment.setting blocks.
ELASTIC_BEANSTALK_MANAGED_UPDATES_ENABLE.title: Elastic Beanstalk environments must enable managed platform updates

ELBV2_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any ALB or NLB with at least one HTTPS / TLS listener whose certificate is missing or whose ARN is not from ACM (or whose ARN is not in AcmCertificatesAllowed).
ELBV2_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.condition_logic: all(l in elbv2.LoadBalancer.Listeners, l.Certificates[0].CertificateArn LIKE 'arn:aws:acm:%') AND (AcmCertificatesAllowed == null OR all(l.Certificates[0].CertificateArn IN AcmCertificatesAllowed))
ELBV2_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers have listeners that are configured to use certificates from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if at least 1 load balancer has at least 1 listener that is configured without a certificate from ACM or is configured with a certificate different from an ACM certificate.
ELBV2_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.remediation_summary: Replace IAM-uploaded or self-issued certificates on every ALB/NLB HTTPS or TLS listener with ACM certificates via aws elbv2 modify-listener --certificates CertificateArn=<acm-arn>, or Terraform aws_lb_listener.certificate_arn = aws_acm_certificate.cert.arn. Restrict to ARNs in AcmCertificatesAllowed when configured.
ELBV2_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.title: ALB and NLB listeners must use ACM certificates

ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ.condition_description: Checks if an Elastic Load Balancer V2 (Application, Network, or Gateway Load Balancer) is mapped to multiple Availability Zones (AZs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Elastic Load Balancer V2 is mapped to less than 2 AZs. For more information, see Availability Zones for your Application Load Balancer. Identifier: ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ Resource Types: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Asia Paci
ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Elastic Load Balancer V2 (Application, Network, or Gateway Load Balancer) is mapped to multiple Availability Zones (AZs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Elastic Load Balancer V2 is mapped to less than 2 AZs. For more information, see Availability Zones for your Application Load Balancer. Identifier: ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ Resource Types: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Asia Paci
ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
ELBV2_MULTIPLE_AZ.title: Elbv2 Multiple Az

ELB_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a Classic Load Balancer with an SSL/HTTPS listener whose SSLCertificateId is not an AWS Certificate Manager ARN.
ELB_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.condition_logic: FOR listener IN classic_lb.Listeners WHERE listener.Protocol IN ['SSL','HTTPS']: starts_with(listener.SSLCertificateId, 'arn:aws:acm:')
ELB_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Classic Load Balancers use SSL certificates provided by AWS Certificate Manager. To use this rule, use an SSL or HTTPS listener with your Classic Load Balancer. This rule is only applicable to Classic Load Balancers. This rule does not check Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers.
ELB_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.remediation_summary: Replace any IAM-uploaded or self-signed certificates on Classic Load Balancer SSL/HTTPS listeners with an ACM-issued certificate ARN. Apply via aws elb set-load-balancer-listener-ssl-certificate or Terraform aws_elb.listeners.ssl_certificate_id pointing at an aws_acm_certificate ARN.
ELB_ACM_CERTIFICATE_REQUIRED.title: Classic Load Balancers must use ACM-issued certificates

ELB_CROSS_ZONE_LOAD_BALANCING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Classic Load Balancer whose CrossZoneLoadBalancing.Enabled attribute is false.
ELB_CROSS_ZONE_LOAD_BALANCING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if cross-zone load balancing is enabled for Classic Load Balancers. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if cross-zone load balancing is not enabled for Classic Load Balancers.
ELB_CROSS_ZONE_LOAD_BALANCING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable cross-zone load balancing on each Classic Load Balancer with aws elb modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-attributes CrossZoneLoadBalancing={Enabled=true}, or Terraform aws_elb.cross_zone_load_balancing = true.
ELB_CROSS_ZONE_LOAD_BALANCING_ENABLED.title: Classic Load Balancers must have cross-zone load balancing enabled

ELB_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Application or Network Load Balancer whose deletion_protection.enabled attribute is false.
ELB_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether an Elastic Load Balancer has deletion protection enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if deletion_protection.enabled is false.
ELB_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Turn on deletion protection on each ALB/NLB via aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn <arn> --attributes Key=deletion_protection.enabled,Value=true, or Terraform aws_lb.enable_deletion_protection = true. Lock down the IAM permission elbv2:ModifyLoadBalancerAttributes to admins.
ELB_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.title: Load balancers must have deletion protection enabled

ELB_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Classic, Application, or v2 load balancer whose access_logs.s3.enabled is false, or whose access_logs.s3.bucket is not in s3BucketNames.
ELB_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: lb.Attributes['access_logs.s3.enabled'] == 'true' AND (s3BucketNames == null OR lb.Attributes['access_logs.s3.bucket'] IN s3BucketNames)
ELB_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Application Load Balancer and the Classic Load Balancer have logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the access_logs.s3.enabled is false or access_logs.S3.bucket is not equal to the s3BucketName that you provided.
ELB_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable S3 access logging on each Classic and Application Load Balancer pointing at a dedicated, encrypted bucket: aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --attributes Key=access_logs.s3.enabled,Value=true Key=access_logs.s3.bucket,Value=<bucket>, or Terraform aws_lb.access_logs { bucket = ... enabled = true }. Allow ELB principals to write to the bucket via the bucket policy.
ELB_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: Load balancers must have access logging enabled

ELB_PREDEFINED_SECURITY_POLICY_SSL_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Classic Load Balancer HTTPS or SSL listener whose policy name does not equal predefinedPolicyName.
ELB_PREDEFINED_SECURITY_POLICY_SSL_CHECK.condition_logic: all(l in elasticloadbalancing.LoadBalancer.Listeners WHERE l.Protocol IN ['HTTPS','SSL'], l.Policies.AppCookieStickinessPolicies[0].PolicyName == predefinedPolicyName OR l.PolicyNames contains predefinedPolicyName)
ELB_PREDEFINED_SECURITY_POLICY_SSL_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Classic Load Balancer SSL listeners use a predefined policy. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Classic Load Balancer HTTPS/SSL listener's policy does not equal the value of the parameter 'predefinedPolicyName'.
ELB_PREDEFINED_SECURITY_POLICY_SSL_CHECK.remediation_summary: Apply the approved predefined SSL security policy (e.g., ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01) to each Classic ELB HTTPS/SSL listener using aws elb set-load-balancer-policies-of-listener, or Terraform aws_load_balancer_policy / aws_load_balancer_listener_policy. Where possible, migrate to ALB/NLB which expose ssl_policy directly.
ELB_PREDEFINED_SECURITY_POLICY_SSL_CHECK.title: Classic Load Balancer SSL listeners must use the approved predefined policy

ELB_TLS_HTTPS_LISTENERS_ONLY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Classic Load Balancer with at least one listener whose Protocol is not HTTPS or SSL.
ELB_TLS_HTTPS_LISTENERS_ONLY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Classic Load Balancer is configured with SSL or HTTPS listeners. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a listener is not configured with SSL or HTTPS.
ELB_TLS_HTTPS_LISTENERS_ONLY.remediation_summary: Replace HTTP / TCP listeners on Classic Load Balancers with HTTPS or SSL listeners (port 443) backed by an ACM or IAM-uploaded certificate via aws elb create-load-balancer-listeners / delete-load-balancer-listeners, or Terraform aws_elb.listener { lb_protocol = "https" ssl_certificate_id = ... }. Migrate to ALB/NLB where feasible.
ELB_TLS_HTTPS_LISTENERS_ONLY.title: Classic Load Balancers must use only HTTPS or SSL listeners

EMR_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if EMR's BlockPublicAccessConfiguration.BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules is false, or if it is true but PermittedPublicSecurityGroupRuleRanges contains ports other than 22.
EMR_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS.condition_logic: emr.BlockPublicAccess.BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules == true AND all(r in emr.BlockPublicAccess.PermittedPublicSecurityGroupRuleRanges, r.MinRange == 22 AND r.MaxRange == 22)
EMR_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an account with Amazon EMR has block public access settings enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules is false, or if true, ports other than Port 22 are listed in PermittedPublicSecurityGroupRuleRanges.
EMR_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS.remediation_summary: Configure EMR account-level block public access via aws emr put-block-public-access-configuration --block-public-access-configuration '{"BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules":true,"PermittedPublicSecurityGroupRuleRanges":[{"MinRange":22,"MaxRange":22}]}', or Terraform aws_emr_block_public_access_configuration.block_public_security_group_rules = true with the only permitted port range 22-22.
EMR_BLOCK_PUBLIC_ACCESS.title: EMR must block public access except SSH on port 22

EMR_KERBEROS_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any EMR cluster lacking a security configuration that enables Kerberos, or whose Kerberos parameters do not match the optional rule parameters.
EMR_KERBEROS_ENABLED.condition_logic: emr.Cluster.SecurityConfiguration.AuthenticationConfiguration.KerberosConfiguration != null AND (TicketLifetimeInHours == null OR Kerberos.TicketLifetimeInHours == TicketLifetimeInHours) AND (Realm == null OR Kerberos.CrossRealmTrustConfiguration.Realm == Realm) AND (Domain == null OR Kerberos.CrossRealmTrustConfiguration.Domain == Domain)
EMR_KERBEROS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon EMR clusters have Kerberos enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a security configuration is not attached to the cluster or the security configuration does not satisfy the specified rule parameters.
EMR_KERBEROS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Create an EMR security configuration that enables Kerberos (KerberosAttributes / AuthenticationConfiguration) and attach it when launching new clusters via aws emr create-security-configuration and aws emr run-job-flow --security-configuration <name> --kerberos-attributes Realm=...,KdcAdminPassword=..., or Terraform aws_emr_security_configuration + aws_emr_cluster.security_configuration / kerberos_attributes.
EMR_KERBEROS_ENABLED.title: EMR clusters must have Kerberos authentication enabled

EMR_MASTER_NO_PUBLIC_IP.condition_description: Periodic rule that inspects each EMR cluster in RUNNING or WAITING state and fails the cluster if any master EC2 instance has a public IPv4 address attached.
EMR_MASTER_NO_PUBLIC_IP.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon EMR clusters' master nodes have public IPs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the master node has a public IP.
EMR_MASTER_NO_PUBLIC_IP.remediation_summary: Launch EMR clusters into private subnets so master nodes do not receive public IPs. Update the cluster's EC2 instance configuration (Instances.Ec2SubnetId) to a private subnet, or recreate the cluster with Terraform aws_emr_cluster.ec2_attributes.subnet_id pointing at a private subnet, and route public traffic via NAT/ALB instead of direct public addressing.
EMR_MASTER_NO_PUBLIC_IP.title: EMR cluster master nodes must not have public IP addresses

ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any attached EBS volume whose Encrypted attribute is false, or whose KmsKeyId does not match the optional kmsId parameter.
ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES.condition_logic: ebs_volume.State == 'in-use' AND ebs_volume.Encrypted == true AND (kmsId == null OR ebs_volume.KmsKeyId == kmsId)
ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES.framework_control_requirement: Checks if attached Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted and optionally are encrypted with a specified KMS key. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if attached EBS volumes are unencrypted or are encrypted with a KMS key not in the supplied parameters.
ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES.remediation_summary: Replace unencrypted EBS volumes with encrypted ones: snapshot the volume, copy the snapshot with --encrypted (and --kms-key-id matching kmsId if specified), create a new volume from the encrypted snapshot, and re-attach. Going forward, enable EBS encryption by default and set encrypted = true, kms_key_id = ... in Terraform aws_ebs_volume / aws_instance.root_block_device.
ENCRYPTED_VOLUMES.title: Attached EBS volumes must be encrypted

FSX_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that verifies each FSx file system (optionally filtered by resourceTags or resourceId) is included in an active AWS Backup plan, and optionally that the backup vault is locked with retention within minRetentionDays/maxRetentionDays.
FSX_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: fsx_file_system IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
FSX_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon FSx File Systems are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon FSx File System is not covered by a backup plan.
FSX_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the FSx file system to an AWS Backup plan via tag-based or resource-based selection. Use the AWS Backup console, aws backup create-backup-selection, or Terraform aws_backup_selection / aws_backup_plan to ensure the file system is covered, and configure a Backup Vault Lock if retention guarantees are required.
FSX_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: Amazon FSx file systems must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

GUARDDUTY_ENABLED_CENTRALIZED.condition_description: Periodic rule that confirms GuardDuty is enabled in the account / region, and optionally that findings are administered from one of the AWS account IDs listed in CentralMonitoringAccount.
GUARDDUTY_ENABLED_CENTRALIZED.condition_logic: guardduty.Detector.Status == 'ENABLED' AND (CentralMonitoringAccount == null OR guardduty.AdminAccountId in CentralMonitoringAccount)
GUARDDUTY_ENABLED_CENTRALIZED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon GuardDuty is enabled in your AWS account and AWS Region. If you provide an AWS account for centralization, the rule evaluates the GuardDuty results in the centralized account. The rule is COMPLIANT when GuardDuty is enabled.
GUARDDUTY_ENABLED_CENTRALIZED.remediation_summary: Enable GuardDuty in every active region via aws guardduty create-detector or Terraform aws_guardduty_detector { enable = true }. To centralize, designate a delegated administrator with aws guardduty enable-organization-admin-account / aws_guardduty_organization_admin_account and add member accounts under that administrator.
GUARDDUTY_ENABLED_CENTRALIZED.title: Amazon GuardDuty must be enabled and optionally centrally administered

GUARDDUTY_NON_ARCHIVED_FINDINGS.condition_description: Periodic rule that flags GuardDuty findings that have been left non-archived for longer than the per-severity threshold (default 30 days low, 7 days medium, 1 day high).
GUARDDUTY_NON_ARCHIVED_FINDINGS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon GuardDuty has findings that are non-archived. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if GuardDuty has non-archived low/medium/high severity findings older than the specified number in the daysLowSev/daysMediumSev/daysHighSev parameter.
GUARDDUTY_NON_ARCHIVED_FINDINGS.remediation_summary: Triage and respond to outstanding GuardDuty findings within the per-severity SLA, then archive them via the GuardDuty console or CLI (aws guardduty archive-findings --detector-id <id> --finding-ids <list>). Tune the daysLowSev/daysMediumSev/daysHighSev parameters only if the operating runbook permits longer remediation windows.
GUARDDUTY_NON_ARCHIVED_FINDINGS.title: GuardDuty findings must be triaged and archived within the configured per-severity window

IAM_CUSTOMER_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that inspects each customer-managed IAM policy and fails the policy if any statement allows a blockedActionsPatterns value (e.g. kms:Decrypt) against Resource '*'. Permission-boundary policies can be excluded via excludePermissionBoundaryPolicy=true.
IAM_CUSTOMER_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.condition_logic: NOT exists(policy.Statement where Effect == 'Allow' AND Action matches blockedActionsPatterns AND Resource == '*') OR (excludePermissionBoundaryPolicy == true AND policy.IsPermissionsBoundary == true)
IAM_CUSTOMER_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the managed AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies that you create do not allow blocked KMS actions on all AWS KMS key resources. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any blocked action is allowed on all AWS KMS keys by the managed IAM policy.
IAM_CUSTOMER_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.remediation_summary: Tighten customer-managed IAM policies so blocked KMS actions (kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey, etc.) are scoped to specific key ARNs rather than '*'. Update the policy via aws iam create-policy-version / set-default-policy-version or Terraform aws_iam_policy.policy with explicit key ARNs in the Resource element, and consider attaching a permission boundary that enforces this constraint.
IAM_CUSTOMER_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.title: IAM customer-managed policies must not allow blocked KMS actions on all KMS keys

IAM_GROUP_HAS_USERS_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that flags an IAM group with zero attached IAM users.
IAM_GROUP_HAS_USERS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether IAM groups have at least one IAM user.
IAM_GROUP_HAS_USERS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Either attach at least one IAM user to the group via the IAM console, CLI (aws iam add-user-to-group --group-name <g> --user-name <u>), or Terraform (aws_iam_user_group_membership / aws_iam_group_membership), or delete the empty group with aws iam delete-group / aws_iam_group resource removal so the access surface stays minimal.
IAM_GROUP_HAS_USERS_CHECK.title: IAM groups must contain at least one IAM user

IAM_INLINE_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that scans inline policies on IAM users, roles, and groups and fails the principal if any statement allows a blockedActionsPatterns value against Resource '*'. Roles only assumable by the organization management account can be excluded via excludeRoleByManagementAccount.
IAM_INLINE_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.condition_logic: NOT exists(inline_policy.Statement where Effect == 'Allow' AND Action matches blockedActionsPatterns AND Resource == '*') OR (excludeRoleByManagementAccount == true AND role.assumable_only_by == 'org-management')
IAM_INLINE_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the inline policies attached to your IAM users, roles, and groups do not allow blocked actions on all AWS KMS keys. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any blocked action is allowed on all AWS KMS keys in an inline policy.
IAM_INLINE_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.remediation_summary: Replace inline IAM policies that grant blocked KMS actions on '*' with managed policies that scope each KMS action to specific key ARNs. Use aws iam delete-user-policy / delete-role-policy / delete-group-policy or Terraform aws_iam_user_policy / aws_iam_role_policy / aws_iam_group_policy to remove the offending statements and reattach least-privilege managed policies in their place.
IAM_INLINE_POLICY_BLOCKED_KMS_ACTIONS.title: IAM inline policies must not allow blocked KMS actions on all KMS keys

IAM_NO_INLINE_POLICY_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any IAM user, role, or group that has at least one inline policy embedded directly on it (vs. an attached managed policy).
IAM_NO_INLINE_POLICY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the inline policy feature is not in use. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) user, IAM role or IAM group has any inline policy.
IAM_NO_INLINE_POLICY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Convert any inline IAM policies on users, roles, and groups into customer managed policies. List inline policies (aws iam list-user-policies / list-role-policies / list-group-policies), recreate them as managed policies (aws iam create-policy), attach with aws iam attach-*-policy, then delete the inline policy. In Terraform, replace aws_iam_*_policy inline blocks with aws_iam_policy + aws_iam_*_policy_attachment.
IAM_NO_INLINE_POLICY_CHECK.title: IAM users, roles, and groups must not have inline policies

IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.condition_description: Periodic rule that retrieves the account password policy and fails if any of the configured length/complexity/age/reuse parameters are weaker than the rule's parameters. Default IAM password policies are NON_COMPLIANT.
IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.condition_logic: policy.MinimumPasswordLength >= MinimumPasswordLength AND policy.RequireUppercaseCharacters == RequireUppercaseCharacters AND policy.RequireLowercaseCharacters == RequireLowercaseCharacters AND policy.RequireSymbols == RequireSymbols AND policy.RequireNumbers == RequireNumbers AND policy.PasswordReusePrevention >= PasswordReusePrevention AND policy.MaxPasswordAge <= MaxPasswordAge
IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the account password policy for AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users meets the specified requirements indicated in the parameters. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the account password policy does not meet the specified requirements.
IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.remediation_summary: Configure the account password policy to meet the minimum length, complexity, reuse-prevention, and rotation requirements. Use aws iam update-account-password-policy with --minimum-password-length 14 --require-uppercase-characters --require-lowercase-characters --require-symbols --require-numbers --password-reuse-prevention 24 --max-password-age 90, or Terraform aws_iam_account_password_policy.
IAM_PASSWORD_POLICY.title: IAM account password policy must meet the configured strength requirements

IAM_POLICY_IN_USE.condition_description: Periodic rule that takes a specific IAM policy ARN and fails the account if that policy is not attached to any IAM user, group with a member, or role with a trust relationship matching the policyUsageType.
IAM_POLICY_IN_USE.condition_logic: (policyUsageType IN [null,'ANY'] AND iam_policy(policyARN).attachment_count > 0) OR (policyUsageType == 'IAM_USER' AND iam_policy(policyARN).attached_user_count > 0) OR (policyUsageType == 'IAM_GROUP' AND iam_policy(policyARN).attached_groups_with_members > 0) OR (policyUsageType == 'IAM_ROLE' AND iam_policy(policyARN).attached_roles_with_trust > 0)
IAM_POLICY_IN_USE.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether the IAM policy ARN is attached to an IAM user, or a group with one or more IAM users, or an IAM role with one or more trusted entity.
IAM_POLICY_IN_USE.remediation_summary: Either attach the specified IAM policy to an appropriate user, group with members, or role with trust relationships, or remove the policy if it is no longer required (aws iam delete-policy after detaching all entities). In Terraform, ensure aws_iam_policy_attachment / aws_iam_role_policy_attachment / aws_iam_user_policy_attachment / aws_iam_group_policy_attachment exist where the policy is intended to be used.
IAM_POLICY_IN_USE.title: Specified IAM policy must be in active use

IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_ADMIN_ACCE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that inspects every customer managed IAM policy version (excluding inline and AWS managed). It fails any policy with a statement that has Effect Allow combined with Action '*' and Resource '*'. Permissions boundaries can be excluded via excludePermissionBoundaryPolicy.
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_ADMIN_ACCE.condition_logic: FOR statement IN customer_managed_policy.statements: NOT (statement.Effect == 'Allow' AND '*' IN statement.Action AND '*' IN statement.Resource)
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_ADMIN_ACCE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies that you create have Allow statements that grant permissions to all actions on all resources. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any customer managed IAM policy statement includes "Effect": "Allow" with "Action": "*" over "Resource": "*".
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_ADMIN_ACCE.remediation_summary: Refactor offending customer managed IAM policies to grant least-privilege access: replace Action '*' / Resource '*' Allow statements with the specific service actions and resource ARNs that the principal actually needs. Use aws iam create-policy-version to publish a corrected default version (or recreate the policy in Terraform aws_iam_policy.policy) and detach AdministratorAccess-equivalent policies from human and service principals.
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_ADMIN_ACCE.title: Customer managed IAM policies must not grant full administrative privileges

IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_FULL_ACCES.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any customer-managed IAM policy whose Statements include an Action of '<service>:*' (for example, ec2:*). Suffixed wildcards such as ec2:Describe* are treated as compliant. Inline and AWS-managed policies are out of scope.
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_FULL_ACCES.condition_logic: NOT exists(policy.Statement where Effect == 'Allow' AND Action matches '^[a-z0-9-]+:\*$') OR (excludePermissionBoundaryPolicy == true AND policy.IsPermissionsBoundary == true)
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_FULL_ACCES.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies that you create grant permissions to all actions on individual AWS resources. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any customer managed IAM policy allows full access to at least 1 AWS service.
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_FULL_ACCES.remediation_summary: Replace service-wide wildcards (e.g. ec2:*) in customer-managed IAM policies with the smallest set of actions required, or with prefixed wildcards (e.g. ec2:Describe*) that group related actions. Edit the policy via aws iam create-policy-version / set-default-policy-version or Terraform aws_iam_policy.policy and attach a permissions boundary that bans full-service wildcards.
IAM_POLICY_NO_STATEMENTS_WITH_FULL_ACCES.title: IAM customer-managed policies must not grant full access to any AWS service

IAM_ROOT_ACCESS_KEY_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that calls IAM GetAccountSummary and fails the account if the root user has any access key, regardless of whether it is active or inactive.
IAM_ROOT_ACCESS_KEY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the root user access key is available. The rule is COMPLIANT if the user access key does not exist. Otherwise, NON_COMPLIANT.
IAM_ROOT_ACCESS_KEY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Sign in as the root user and delete every root access key from the My Security Credentials page (or via aws iam delete-access-key while signed in as root). Provision IAM users or IAM Identity Center principals for day-to-day use and never recreate root keys.
IAM_ROOT_ACCESS_KEY_CHECK.title: Root user must not have any access keys

IAM_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any IAM user that is not a member of any IAM group, and (if groupNames is set) any user not in at least one of the listed groups.
IAM_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK.condition_logic: len(iam_user.Groups) > 0 AND (groupNames == null OR iam_user.Groups intersects groupNames)
IAM_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether IAM users are members of at least one IAM group.
IAM_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK.remediation_summary: Add each IAM user to at least one IAM group that holds their permissions. Use aws iam add-user-to-group or Terraform aws_iam_user_group_membership / aws_iam_group_membership. Manage permissions through groups rather than user-attached policies so access can be governed centrally.
IAM_USER_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK.title: IAM users must be members of at least one IAM group

IAM_USER_MFA_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that verifies each IAM user has at least one MFA device enrolled (virtual or hardware). Users without an MFA device fail the rule.
IAM_USER_MFA_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if MFA is not enabled for at least one IAM user.
IAM_USER_MFA_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enroll an MFA device for every IAM user with console access. Use aws iam enable-mfa-device after provisioning a virtual or hardware token, or apply Terraform aws_iam_virtual_mfa_device. Enforce sign-in MFA via an IAM policy condition (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent) and consider replacing long-lived IAM users with IAM Identity Center / IAM roles where possible.
IAM_USER_MFA_ENABLED.title: IAM users must have multi-factor authentication enabled

IAM_USER_NO_POLICIES_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an IAM user who has any managed policy attached directly or any inline policy attached; users must instead inherit permissions through group or role membership.
IAM_USER_NO_POLICIES_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if none of your AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users have policies attached. IAM users must inherit permissions from IAM groups or roles. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there is at least one policy that is attached to the IAM user.
IAM_USER_NO_POLICIES_CHECK.remediation_summary: Detach all managed policies and delete inline policies on IAM users. Move the user into IAM groups (or replace their use with IAM roles) that hold the managed policies instead. Use aws iam detach-user-policy / delete-user-policy / add-user-to-group, or Terraform aws_iam_group_membership / aws_iam_user_policy_attachment refactored onto aws_iam_group_policy_attachment.
IAM_USER_NO_POLICIES_CHECK.title: IAM users must not have policies attached directly

IAM_USER_UNUSED_CREDENTIALS_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any IAM user whose console password or active access key has not been used within maxCredentialUsageAge days (default 90). Inactive credentials still count if the user owns them.
IAM_USER_UNUSED_CREDENTIALS_CHECK.condition_logic: (now - iam_user.password_last_used).days <= maxCredentialUsageAge AND ALL access_key IN iam_user.active_access_keys: (now - access_key.last_used).days <= maxCredentialUsageAge
IAM_USER_UNUSED_CREDENTIALS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users have passwords or active access keys that have not been used within the specified number of days you provided. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are inactive accounts not recently used.
IAM_USER_UNUSED_CREDENTIALS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Review the IAM credential report and disable or delete any console password or access key not used within maxCredentialUsageAge days. Use aws iam delete-login-profile, aws iam update-access-key --status Inactive (then delete), or refactor Terraform to remove aws_iam_user / aws_iam_access_key resources for unused identities.
IAM_USER_UNUSED_CREDENTIALS_CHECK.title: IAM user credentials unused beyond the maximum age must be removed

INTERNET_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZED_VPC_ONLY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any internet gateway attached to a VPC whose ID is not in the AuthorizedVpcIds allow list. If the parameter is empty, all attached IGWs are non-compliant.
INTERNET_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZED_VPC_ONLY.condition_logic: AuthorizedVpcIds != null AND ALL attachment IN igw.Attachments: attachment.VpcId IN AuthorizedVpcIds
INTERNET_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZED_VPC_ONLY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if internet gateways are attached to an authorized virtual private cloud (Amazon VPC). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if internet gateways are attached to an unauthorized VPC.
INTERNET_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZED_VPC_ONLY.remediation_summary: Detach internet gateways from any VPC not on the AuthorizedVpcIds list (aws ec2 detach-internet-gateway) or delete unused IGWs (aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway). In Terraform, remove aws_internet_gateway resources or aws_internet_gateway_attachment associations for VPCs that should not have direct internet egress.
INTERNET_GATEWAY_AUTHORIZED_VPC_ONLY.title: Internet gateways must be attached only to authorized VPCs

KINESIS_STREAM_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Kinesis data stream whose StreamDescription.EncryptionType is NONE (i.e., the StreamEncryption block is absent).
KINESIS_STREAM_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Kinesis streams are encrypted at rest with server-side encryption. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a Kinesis stream if 'StreamEncryption' is not present.
KINESIS_STREAM_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Enable server-side encryption on each Kinesis data stream with a KMS key using aws kinesis start-stream-encryption --encryption-type KMS --key-id <kms-arn>, or Terraform aws_kinesis_stream.encryption_type = "KMS" and kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.x.arn.
KINESIS_STREAM_ENCRYPTED.title: Kinesis Data Streams must be encrypted at rest with KMS

KMS_CMK_NOT_SCHEDULED_FOR_DELETION.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any customer-managed KMS key whose KeyState is PendingDeletion. Optionally only the keys listed in kmsKeyIds are evaluated.
KMS_CMK_NOT_SCHEDULED_FOR_DELETION.condition_logic: kms_key.KeyState != 'PendingDeletion' AND (kmsKeyIds == null OR kms_key.KeyId in kmsKeyIds)
KMS_CMK_NOT_SCHEDULED_FOR_DELETION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys are not scheduled for deletion in AWS KMS. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if KMS keys are scheduled for deletion.
KMS_CMK_NOT_SCHEDULED_FOR_DELETION.remediation_summary: Cancel any pending KMS key deletion before the waiting period elapses. Use aws kms cancel-key-deletion --key-id <id> or remove the deletion_window_in_days configuration in Terraform aws_kms_key, then re-enable the key with aws kms enable-key. Migrate dependent resources to a replacement key before scheduling deletion in the future.
KMS_CMK_NOT_SCHEDULED_FOR_DELETION.title: Customer-managed KMS keys must not be scheduled for deletion

LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if the Lambda function is configured with a function-level concurrent execution limit. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not configured with a function-level concurrent execution limit. Identifier: LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: ConcurrencyLimitHigh (Optional) Type: String Maximum concurrency execution limit ConcurrencyLimitLow (Optional) Type: String Minimum concurrency execution limit
LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Lambda function is configured with a function-level concurrent execution limit. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not configured with a function-level concurrent execution limit. Identifier: LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: ConcurrencyLimitHigh (Optional) Type: String Maximum concurrency execution limit ConcurrencyLimitLow (Optional) Type: String Minimum concurrency execution limit
LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
LAMBDA_CONCURRENCY_CHECK.title: Lambda Concurrency Check

LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK.condition_description: Checks whether an AWS Lambda function is configured with a dead-letter queue. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not configured with a dead-letter queue. Identifier: LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: dlqArns (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS ARNs that must be configured as the Lambda function dead-letter queue target
LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether an AWS Lambda function is configured with a dead-letter queue. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not configured with a dead-letter queue. Identifier: LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: dlqArns (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS ARNs that must be configured as the Lambda function dead-letter queue target
LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
LAMBDA_DLQ_CHECK.title: Lambda Dlq Check

LAMBDA_FUNCTION_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Lambda function whose resource-based policy includes a statement granting access to a wildcard or empty Principal, or to anonymous S3 invocations without an AWS:SourceAccount condition.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: NOT exists(lambda.Policy.Statement where Principal == '*' OR Principal.AWS == '*' OR Principal == {} OR (Principal.Service == 's3.amazonaws.com' AND NOT Condition contains 'AWS:SourceAccount'))
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the AWS Lambda function policy attached to the Lambda resource prohibits public access. If the Lambda function policy allows public access it is NON_COMPLIANT.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Lock down each Lambda function's resource policy so only specific AWS accounts, principals, or services can invoke it. Use aws lambda remove-permission to delete public statements and aws lambda add-permission with an explicit Principal (or Terraform aws_lambda_permission with principal and source_account/source_arn) to grant least-privilege access.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.title: Lambda function resource policies must prohibit public access

LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Lambda functions (excluding container-image and OS-only runtimes) when the Runtime, Role, MemorySize, or Timeout settings do not match the configured parameters.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK.condition_logic: lambda.Runtime in runtime AND (role == null OR lambda.Role == role) AND lambda.MemorySize == memorySize AND lambda.Timeout == timeout
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the AWS Lambda function settings for runtime, role, timeout, and memory size match the expected values. The rule ignores functions with the 'Image' package type and functions with runtime set to 'OS-only Runtime'. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function settings do not match the expected values.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Update each Lambda function so it uses an approved runtime version and the expected execution role, memory size, and timeout. Apply changes with aws lambda update-function-configuration or Terraform aws_lambda_function (runtime, role, memory_size, timeout) and add CI policy to block deployments on unsupported runtimes.
LAMBDA_FUNCTION_SETTINGS_CHECK.title: Lambda functions must use approved runtime, role, memory, and timeout settings

LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC.condition_description: Checks if a Lambda function is allowed access to a virtual private cloud (VPC). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not VPC enabled. Identifier: LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: subnetIds (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of subnet IDs that Lambda functions must be associated with.
LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a Lambda function is allowed access to a virtual private cloud (VPC). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Lambda function is not VPC enabled. Identifier: LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except China (Ningxia) Region Parameters: subnetIds (Optional) Type: CSV Comma-separated list of subnet IDs that Lambda functions must be associated with.
LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
LAMBDA_INSIDE_VPC.title: Lambda Inside Vpc

LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if Lambda has more than 1 availability zone associated. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if only 1 availability zone is associated with the Lambda or the number of availability zones associated is less than number specified in the optional parameter. Identifier: LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), China (Ningxia) Region Paramete
LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Lambda has more than 1 availability zone associated. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if only 1 availability zone is associated with the Lambda or the number of availability zones associated is less than number specified in the optional parameter. Identifier: LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Lambda::Function Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), China (Ningxia) Region Paramete
LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
LAMBDA_VPC_MULTI_AZ_CHECK.title: Lambda Vpc Multi Az Check

MACIE_AUTO_SENSITIVE_DATA_DISCOVERY_CHEC.condition_description: Periodic rule executed in the Macie administrator account that fails if automated sensitive data discovery is disabled. Member accounts evaluate as NOT_APPLICABLE.
MACIE_AUTO_SENSITIVE_DATA_DISCOVERY_CHEC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if automated sensitive data discovery is enabled for Amazon Macie. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if automated sensitive data discovery is disabled. The rule is APPLICABLE for administrator accounts and NOT_APPLICABLE for member accounts.
MACIE_AUTO_SENSITIVE_DATA_DISCOVERY_CHEC.remediation_summary: In the Macie administrator account, enable automated sensitive data discovery with aws macie2 update-automated-discovery-configuration --status ENABLED, or via Terraform aws_macie2_account combined with the automated discovery configuration setting in the AWS console. Configure scope and S3 bucket inclusions/exclusions to control cost.
MACIE_AUTO_SENSITIVE_DATA_DISCOVERY_CHEC.title: Amazon Macie automated sensitive data discovery must be enabled

MACIE_STATUS_CHECK.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account/region pair if Macie's account-level status attribute is not 'ENABLED'.
MACIE_STATUS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Macie is enabled in your account per region. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the 'status' attribute is not set to 'ENABLED'.
MACIE_STATUS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Enable Macie in each region via aws macie2 enable-macie or Terraform aws_macie2_account.status = "ENABLED". Use the delegated administrator pattern through AWS Organizations to manage Macie centrally and configure default S3 bucket scoping.
MACIE_STATUS_CHECK.title: Amazon Macie must be enabled in every account and region

MFA_ENABLED_FOR_IAM_CONSOLE_ACCESS.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any IAM user with a console password whose account does not have at least one virtual or hardware MFA device enabled.
MFA_ENABLED_FOR_IAM_CONSOLE_ACCESS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users that use a console password. The rule is COMPLIANT if MFA is enabled.
MFA_ENABLED_FOR_IAM_CONSOLE_ACCESS.remediation_summary: For every IAM user with a console password, enroll a virtual or hardware MFA device using aws iam enable-mfa-device (or the IAM console > Security credentials), or migrate users to IAM Identity Center where MFA is enforced. Disable console access (aws iam delete-login-profile) for service accounts that don't need it.
MFA_ENABLED_FOR_IAM_CONSOLE_ACCESS.title: IAM users with console access must have MFA enabled

MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that inspects each Amazon MQ broker and fails the broker if audit logging to CloudWatch Logs is disabled in the Logs configuration.
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon MQ brokers have Amazon CloudWatch audit logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a broker does not have audit logging enabled.
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable audit logging on each Amazon MQ broker by setting the Logs.Audit configuration to true. Use aws mq update-broker --logs Audit=true or Terraform aws_mq_broker.logs { audit = true } and grant the broker the IAM permissions needed to write to CloudWatch Logs.
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: Amazon MQ brokers must enable CloudWatch audit logging

MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an Amazon MQ broker whenever its configuration is updated without enabling Logs.Audit (CloudWatch audit logging).
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon MQ broker has CloudWatch audit logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the broker does not have audit logging enabled.
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable audit logging on each Amazon MQ broker. Use aws mq update-broker --logs Audit=true or Terraform aws_mq_broker.logs { audit = true } so the broker streams authentication and management events to CloudWatch Logs for review.
MQ_CLOUDWATCH_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED.title: Amazon MQ brokers must enable CloudWatch audit logging (configuration-change variant)

MSK_IN_CLUSTER_NODE_REQUIRE_TLS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any MSK cluster whose EncryptionInfo.EncryptionInTransit.InCluster is not true (i.e., plaintext broker-to-broker traffic is permitted).
MSK_IN_CLUSTER_NODE_REQUIRE_TLS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon MSK cluster enforces encryption in transit using HTTPS (TLS) with the broker nodes of the cluster. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if plain text communication is enabled for in-cluster broker node connections.
MSK_IN_CLUSTER_NODE_REQUIRE_TLS.remediation_summary: Recreate the MSK cluster with EncryptionInTransit.InCluster=true. Use aws kafka update-cluster-configuration with the corrected encryption settings, or Terraform aws_msk_cluster.encryption_info { encryption_in_transit { in_cluster = true, client_broker = "TLS" } }, then migrate clients to TLS endpoints (port 9094).
MSK_IN_CLUSTER_NODE_REQUIRE_TLS.title: Amazon MSK clusters must require TLS for in-cluster broker traffic

MULTI_REGION_CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that requires at least one CloudTrail trail with IsMultiRegionTrail set to true that is logging, optionally matching the supplied S3 bucket, SNS topic, CloudWatch Logs group, includeManagementEvents flag, and readWriteType. Trails that exclude management event sources (e.g., KMS, RDS Data API) are non-compliant.
MULTI_REGION_CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.condition_logic: EXISTS trail WHERE trail.IsMultiRegionTrail == true AND trail.IsLogging == true AND trail.EventSelectors.IncludeManagementEvents == true AND len(trail.EventSelectors.ExcludeManagementEventSources) == 0 AND (s3BucketName == null OR trail.S3BucketName == s3BucketName) AND (snsTopicArn == null OR trail.SnsTopicArn == snsTopicArn) AND (cloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn == null OR trail.CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn == cloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn) AND (readWriteType == null OR trail.EventSelectors.ReadWriteType == readWriteType)
MULTI_REGION_CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if there is at least one multi-region AWS CloudTrail. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the trails do not match input parameters. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the ExcludeManagementEventSources field is not empty or if AWS CloudTrail is configured to exclude management events such as AWS KMS events or Amazon RDS Data API events.
MULTI_REGION_CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Provision (or update) one CloudTrail trail with IsMultiRegionTrail = true that captures all management events (no ExcludeManagementEventSources) and reads/writes (ReadWriteType = All). Apply via aws cloudtrail update-trail --is-multi-region-trail --include-global-service-events / put-event-selectors, or Terraform aws_cloudtrail.is_multi_region_trail = true with aws_cloudtrail.event_selector blocks that include management events.
MULTI_REGION_CLOUDTRAIL_ENABLED.title: At least one multi-Region CloudTrail must be enabled and capture all management events

NACL_NO_UNRESTRICTED_SSH_RDP.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any network ACL with an inbound entry whose CIDR is unrestricted (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0) and whose port range covers TCP/UDP 22 (SSH) or 3389 (RDP).
NACL_NO_UNRESTRICTED_SSH_RDP.condition_logic: FOR entry IN nacl.Entries WHERE entry.Egress == false AND entry.RuleAction == 'allow' AND entry.CidrBlock IN ['0.0.0.0/0','::/0'] AND entry.Protocol IN ['tcp','udp','-1']: NOT (entry.PortRange.From <= 22 AND entry.PortRange.To >= 22) AND NOT (entry.PortRange.From <= 3389 AND entry.PortRange.To >= 3389)
NACL_NO_UNRESTRICTED_SSH_RDP.framework_control_requirement: Checks if default ports for SSH/RDP ingress traffic for network access control lists (NACLs) is unrestricted. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a NACL inbound entry allows a source TCP or UDP CIDR block for ports 22 or 3389.
NACL_NO_UNRESTRICTED_SSH_RDP.remediation_summary: Remove or scope-down any inbound NACL rule that allows 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to TCP/UDP 22 or 3389. Use aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry / delete-network-acl-entry, or Terraform aws_network_acl_rule (and the ingress block of aws_network_acl) to restrict source CIDRs to corporate or bastion ranges.
NACL_NO_UNRESTRICTED_SSH_RDP.title: Network ACLs must not allow unrestricted ingress to SSH or RDP

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_BACKUP_RETENTION_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Neptune DB clusters whose BackupRetentionPeriod is less than minimumBackupRetentionPeriod (default 7, max 35 days).
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_BACKUP_RETENTION_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Neptune DB cluster retention period is set to specific number of days. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the retention period is less than the value specified by the parameter.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_BACKUP_RETENTION_CHECK.remediation_summary: Increase the BackupRetentionPeriod on each Neptune DB cluster to at least the required minimum (default 7 days). Use aws neptune modify-db-cluster --backup-retention-period <days> or Terraform aws_neptune_cluster.backup_retention_period and ensure the change is applied within the next maintenance window.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_BACKUP_RETENTION_CHECK.title: Amazon Neptune DB cluster backup retention must meet the minimum

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_EXPORT_EN.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Neptune clusters whose EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports does not include 'audit'.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_EXPORT_EN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Neptune cluster has CloudWatch log export enabled for audit logs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a Neptune cluster does not have CloudWatch log export enabled for audit logs.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_EXPORT_EN.remediation_summary: Enable audit log export to CloudWatch on each Neptune cluster via aws neptune modify-db-cluster --cloudwatch-logs-export-configuration EnableLogTypes=audit, or Terraform aws_neptune_cluster.enable_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["audit"]. Ensure the cluster parameter group sets neptune_enable_audit_log = 1.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_CLOUDWATCH_LOG_EXPORT_EN.title: Amazon Neptune clusters must export audit logs to CloudWatch Logs

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Neptune DB cluster whose StorageEncrypted flag is false. If KmsKeyArns is supplied, the cluster must additionally be encrypted with one of those keys.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.condition_logic: neptune_cluster.StorageEncrypted == true AND (KmsKeyArns == null OR neptune_cluster.KmsKeyId in KmsKeyArns)
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if storage encryption is enabled for your Amazon Neptune DB clusters. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if storage encryption is not enabled.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Recreate the Neptune cluster with StorageEncrypted=true and (optionally) the desired KMS key. Take a snapshot of the unencrypted cluster, copy the snapshot with KmsKeyId set, and restore it via aws neptune restore-db-cluster-from-snapshot or Terraform aws_neptune_cluster.storage_encrypted / kms_key_arn.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_ENCRYPTED.title: Amazon Neptune DB clusters must enable storage encryption

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_IAM_DATABASE_AUTHENTICAT.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Neptune cluster whose IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled flag is false.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_IAM_DATABASE_AUTHENTICAT.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Neptune cluster has AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) database authentication enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Amazon Neptune cluster does not have IAM database authentication enabled.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_IAM_DATABASE_AUTHENTICAT.remediation_summary: Enable IAM database authentication on each Neptune cluster via aws neptune modify-db-cluster --enable-iam-database-authentication or Terraform aws_neptune_cluster.iam_database_authentication_enabled = true. Update applications to obtain auth tokens with rds:Connect IAM permissions instead of static passwords.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_IAM_DATABASE_AUTHENTICAT.title: Amazon Neptune clusters must enable IAM database authentication

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Neptune DB cluster snapshot whose StorageEncrypted flag is false.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Neptune DB cluster has snapshots encrypted. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a Neptune cluster does not have snapshots encrypted.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Encrypt Neptune cluster snapshots by copying each unencrypted snapshot with a KMS key (aws neptune copy-db-cluster-snapshot --kms-key-id <key>) and deleting the unencrypted original. Going forward, ensure source clusters are encrypted with aws_neptune_cluster.storage_encrypted = true so all derived snapshots inherit encryption.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.title: Amazon Neptune cluster snapshots must be encrypted at rest

NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBIT.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any manual Neptune cluster snapshot whose AttributeName 'restore' includes 'all' (publicly shared).
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBIT.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Neptune manual DB cluster snapshot is public. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any existing and new Neptune cluster snapshot is public.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBIT.remediation_summary: Remove the 'all' value from the snapshot's restore attribute via aws neptune modify-db-cluster-snapshot-attribute --attribute-name restore --values-to-remove all, or remove public sharing in Terraform with aws_db_cluster_snapshot. Audit downstream automation that may have shared the snapshot publicly.
NEPTUNE_CLUSTER_SNAPSHOT_PUBLIC_PROHIBIT.title: Amazon Neptune cluster snapshots must not be public

NETFW_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any Network Firewall LoggingConfiguration that does not enable the requested log type ('alert', 'flow', or 'both').
NETFW_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: (logType == null AND len(firewall.LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs) > 0) OR (logType == 'both' AND {'ALERT','FLOW'} subset firewall.LoggingConfiguration.LogTypes) OR (logType.upper() in firewall.LoggingConfiguration.LogTypes)
NETFW_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Network Firewall firewalls have logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a logging type is not configured. You can specify which logging type you want the rule to check.
NETFW_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure logging on each Network Firewall via aws network-firewall update-logging-configuration or Terraform aws_networkfirewall_logging_configuration with both ALERT and FLOW log types directed to CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Kinesis Data Firehose. Apply IAM permissions for the firewall to write to the destination.
NETFW_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: AWS Network Firewall logging must be enabled

NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FRAGMENT_PAC.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a Network Firewall policy whose StatelessFragmentDefaultActions field does not equal the configured statelessFragmentDefaultActions parameter list.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FRAGMENT_PAC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS Network Firewall policy is configured with a user defined stateless default action for fragmented packets. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if stateless default action for fragmented packets does not match with user defined default action.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FRAGMENT_PAC.remediation_summary: Update the Network Firewall policy so its stateless fragment default actions match the approved list (e.g. aws:drop or aws:forward_to_sfe). Use aws network-firewall update-firewall-policy or Terraform aws_networkfirewall_firewall_policy.firewall_policy.stateless_fragment_default_actions to set the value.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FRAGMENT_PAC.title: Network Firewall stateless default action for fragmented packets must match policy

NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FULL_PACKETS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a Network Firewall policy whose StatelessDefaultActions field does not equal the configured statelessDefaultActions parameter list.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FULL_PACKETS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS Network Firewall policy is configured with a user defined default stateless action for full packets. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if default stateless action for full packets does not match with user defined default stateless action.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FULL_PACKETS.remediation_summary: Update the Network Firewall policy so its stateless default actions for full packets match the approved list (e.g. aws:drop or aws:forward_to_sfe). Apply via aws network-firewall update-firewall-policy or Terraform aws_networkfirewall_firewall_policy.firewall_policy.stateless_default_actions.
NETFW_POLICY_DEFAULT_ACTION_FULL_PACKETS.title: Network Firewall stateless default action for full packets must match policy

NETFW_POLICY_RULE_GROUP_ASSOCIATED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that flags any AWS Network Firewall policy with no stateful and no stateless rule-group associations attached.
NETFW_POLICY_RULE_GROUP_ASSOCIATED.framework_control_requirement: Check AWS Network Firewall policy is associated with stateful OR stateless rule groups. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if no stateful or stateless rule groups are associated with the Network Firewall policy else COMPLIANT if any one of the rule group exists.
NETFW_POLICY_RULE_GROUP_ASSOCIATED.remediation_summary: Associate at least one stateful or stateless rule group with the Network Firewall policy via the Network Firewall console, CLI (aws network-firewall update-firewall-policy), or Terraform aws_networkfirewall_firewall_policy resource (stateful_rule_group_reference / stateless_rule_group_references blocks).
NETFW_POLICY_RULE_GROUP_ASSOCIATED.title: AWS Network Firewall policies must reference at least one rule group

NETFW_STATELESS_RULE_GROUP_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that flags any AWS Network Firewall stateless rule group with zero stateless rules defined.
NETFW_STATELESS_RULE_GROUP_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a Stateless Network Firewall Rule Group contains rules. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are no rules in a Stateless Network Firewall Rule Group.
NETFW_STATELESS_RULE_GROUP_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Add one or more stateless rules to the Network Firewall stateless rule group via the console, CLI (aws network-firewall update-rule-group --type STATELESS), or Terraform aws_networkfirewall_rule_group (rule_group.rules_source.stateless_rules_and_custom_actions block); or delete the empty group if no longer needed.
NETFW_STATELESS_RULE_GROUP_NOT_EMPTY.title: AWS Network Firewall stateless rule groups must contain at least one rule

NO_UNRESTRICTED_ROUTE_TO_IGW.condition_description: Configuration-change and periodic rule that fails route tables containing a route whose target is an internet-gateway and whose destination CIDR is 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, unless the route table id is in routeTableIds.
NO_UNRESTRICTED_ROUTE_TO_IGW.condition_logic: NOT exists(route in route_table.Routes where route.GatewayId starts_with 'igw-' AND route.DestinationCidrBlock in ['0.0.0.0/0','::/0']) OR route_table.RouteTableId in routeTableIds
NO_UNRESTRICTED_ROUTE_TO_IGW.framework_control_requirement: Checks if there are public routes in the route table to an Internet gateway (IGW). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a route to an IGW has a destination CIDR block of '0.0.0.0/0' or '::/0' or if a destination CIDR block does not match the rule parameter.
NO_UNRESTRICTED_ROUTE_TO_IGW.remediation_summary: Restrict 0.0.0.0/0 routes through an Internet gateway to dedicated public route tables / public subnets only. Remove the route from private route tables via aws ec2 delete-route or Terraform aws_route, and rely on NAT gateways or VPC endpoints for outbound private traffic.
NO_UNRESTRICTED_ROUTE_TO_IGW.title: Route tables must not have unrestricted routes to an Internet gateway
