OPENSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any OpenSearch domain whose EncryptionAtRestOptions.Enabled is false. Elasticsearch domains are out of scope.
OPENSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon OpenSearch Service domains have encryption at rest configuration enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the EncryptionAtRestOptions field is not enabled.
OPENSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.remediation_summary: Recreate the OpenSearch domain with encryption at rest enabled. Take a manual snapshot, then use aws opensearch create-domain with EncryptionAtRestOptions.Enabled=true (and a KmsKeyId), or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.encrypt_at_rest { enabled = true, kms_key_id = ... } and reindex from the snapshot.
OPENSEARCH_ENCRYPTED_AT_REST.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service domains must enable encryption at rest

OPENSEARCH_HTTPS_REQUIRED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails OpenSearch domains where DomainEndpointOptions.EnforceHTTPS is not true, or where TLSSecurityPolicy is not in the tlsPolicies parameter list when supplied.
OPENSEARCH_HTTPS_REQUIRED.condition_logic: opensearch_domain.DomainEndpointOptions.EnforceHTTPS == true AND (tlsPolicies == null OR opensearch_domain.DomainEndpointOptions.TLSSecurityPolicy in tlsPolicies)
OPENSEARCH_HTTPS_REQUIRED.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether connections to OpenSearch domains are using HTTPS. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon OpenSearch domain 'EnforceHTTPS' is not 'true' or is 'true' and 'TLSSecurityPolicy' is not in 'tlsPolicies'.
OPENSEARCH_HTTPS_REQUIRED.remediation_summary: Update each OpenSearch domain's domain-endpoint options to require HTTPS and a modern TLS policy (e.g. Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-2019-07). Use aws opensearch update-domain-config --domain-endpoint-options EnforceHTTPS=true,TLSSecurityPolicy=Policy-Min-TLS-1-2-2019-07 or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.domain_endpoint_options.
OPENSEARCH_HTTPS_REQUIRED.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service domains must enforce HTTPS-only connections

OPENSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails OpenSearch domains whose endpoint is publicly accessible (no VPC configuration). Elasticsearch domains are out of scope.
OPENSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon OpenSearch Service domains are in an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an OpenSearch Service domain endpoint is public.
OPENSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.remediation_summary: Recreate the OpenSearch domain inside a VPC. Take a snapshot, create a new domain with aws opensearch create-domain --vpc-options SubnetIds=...,SecurityGroupIds=... or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.vpc_options, restore from snapshot, and decommission the public domain. Use VPC endpoints / private DNS for client access.
OPENSEARCH_IN_VPC_ONLY.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service domains must reside in a VPC

OPENSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails OpenSearch domains whose LogPublishingOptions does not include the required log types (search, index, error). When logTypes is supplied, every listed type must be enabled.
OPENSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.condition_logic: (logTypes == null AND len(opensearch_domain.LogPublishingOptions) > 0) OR (every t in logTypes : opensearch_domain.LogPublishingOptions[t].Enabled == true)
OPENSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon OpenSearch Service domains are configured to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if logging is not configured.
OPENSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.remediation_summary: Enable log publishing on each OpenSearch domain for SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS, INDEX_SLOW_LOGS, and ES_APPLICATION_LOGS to a dedicated CloudWatch Logs log group. Use aws opensearch update-domain-config --log-publishing-options or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.log_publishing_options blocks per log type.
OPENSEARCH_LOGS_TO_CLOUDWATCH.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service domains must send logs to CloudWatch Logs

OPENSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails OpenSearch domains whose NodeToNodeEncryptionOptions.Enabled is false. Elasticsearch domains are out of scope.
OPENSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Check if Amazon OpenSearch Service nodes are encrypted end to end. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the node-to-node encryption is not enabled on the domain.
OPENSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CHECK.remediation_summary: Recreate the OpenSearch domain with node-to-node encryption enabled (this property cannot be enabled in place). Snapshot the existing data, create a new domain via aws opensearch create-domain --node-to-node-encryption-options Enabled=true or Terraform aws_opensearch_domain.node_to_node_encryption { enabled = true }, and reindex.
OPENSEARCH_NODE_TO_NODE_ENCRYPTION_CHECK.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service domains must enable node-to-node encryption

RDS_AUTOMATIC_MINOR_VERSION_UPGRADE_ENAB.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB instances whose AutoMinorVersionUpgrade flag is false.
RDS_AUTOMATIC_MINOR_VERSION_UPGRADE_ENAB.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) database instances are configured for automatic minor version upgrades. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the value of 'autoMinorVersionUpgrade' is false.
RDS_AUTOMATIC_MINOR_VERSION_UPGRADE_ENAB.remediation_summary: Enable automatic minor version upgrades on each RDS instance via aws rds modify-db-instance --auto-minor-version-upgrade --apply-immediately, or Terraform aws_db_instance.auto_minor_version_upgrade = true. Verify the maintenance window is set to a low-traffic period.
RDS_AUTOMATIC_MINOR_VERSION_UPGRADE_ENAB.title: RDS DB instances must enable automatic minor version upgrades

The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the admin username is set to the default value. RDS_CLUSTER_DEFAULT_ADMIN_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) database cluster has changed the admin username from its default value. RDS_CLUSTER_DEFAULT_ADMIN_CHECK.title: Rds Cluster Default Admin Check

RDS_CLUSTER_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB cluster whose DeletionProtection flag is false.
RDS_CLUSTER_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) cluster has deletion protection enabled. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an RDS cluster does not have deletion protection enabled.
RDS_CLUSTER_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable deletion protection on each RDS DB cluster via aws rds modify-db-cluster --deletion-protection or Terraform aws_rds_cluster.deletion_protection = true. Combine with strict IAM policies that deny rds:DeleteDBCluster from non-administrative principals.
RDS_CLUSTER_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.title: RDS DB clusters must have deletion protection enabled

RDS_CLUSTER_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB clusters whose IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled is false.
RDS_CLUSTER_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) cluster has AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Amazon RDS Cluster does not have IAM authentication enabled.
RDS_CLUSTER_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable IAM authentication on each RDS DB cluster via aws rds modify-db-cluster --enable-iam-database-authentication or Terraform aws_rds_cluster.iam_database_authentication_enabled = true. Update applications to fetch short-lived auth tokens via rds-db:connect IAM permissions instead of static passwords.
RDS_CLUSTER_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.title: RDS DB clusters must enable IAM database authentication

RDS_CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB clusters whose MultiAZ flag is false (Aurora and Multi-AZ DB clusters).
RDS_CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Multi-Availability Zone (Multi-AZ) replication is enabled on Amazon Aurora and Multi-AZ DB clusters managed by Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Amazon RDS instance is not configured with Multi-AZ.
RDS_CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable Multi-AZ on each RDS DB cluster. For Aurora, add at least one reader in another AZ via aws rds create-db-instance or Terraform aws_rds_cluster_instance across multiple availability_zones. For Multi-AZ DB clusters, set --multi-az on aws rds create-db-cluster / aws_rds_cluster.
RDS_CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ_ENABLED.title: RDS DB clusters must have Multi-AZ replication enabled

RDS_DB_SECURITY_GROUP_NOT_ALLOWED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any non-default RDS DB security group (the legacy EC2-Classic style RDS security group). Modern RDS deployments should use VPC security groups exclusively.
RDS_DB_SECURITY_GROUP_NOT_ALLOWED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if there are any Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) DB security groups that are not the default DB security group. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are any DB security groups that are not the default DB security group.
RDS_DB_SECURITY_GROUP_NOT_ALLOWED.remediation_summary: Migrate any RDS DB instances still using non-default RDS DB security groups onto VPC-based aws_security_group resources, then delete the legacy DB security groups via aws rds delete-db-security-group. New RDS instances should be deployed inside a VPC subnet group with VPC security groups attached.
RDS_DB_SECURITY_GROUP_NOT_ALLOWED.title: RDS DB security groups other than the default must not exist

RDS_ENHANCED_MONITORING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB instances whose MonitoringInterval is 0 (disabled), or, when supplied, does not equal monitoringInterval (valid values 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60).
RDS_ENHANCED_MONITORING_ENABLED.condition_logic: rds_db_instance.MonitoringInterval > 0 AND (monitoringInterval == null OR rds_db_instance.MonitoringInterval == monitoringInterval)
RDS_ENHANCED_MONITORING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if enhanced monitoring is enabled for Amazon RDS instances. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'monitoringInterval' is '0' in the configuration item of the RDS instance, or if 'monitoringInterval' does not match the rule parameter value.
RDS_ENHANCED_MONITORING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable Enhanced Monitoring on each RDS instance with a non-zero MonitoringInterval (typically 60 seconds). Use aws rds modify-db-instance --monitoring-interval 60 --monitoring-role-arn <role>, or Terraform aws_db_instance.monitoring_interval and monitoring_role_arn pointing at an IAM role with the AmazonRDSEnhancedMonitoringRole policy.
RDS_ENHANCED_MONITORING_ENABLED.title: RDS DB instances must enable Enhanced Monitoring

Warning Some RDS DB instances within a Cluster (Aurora/DocumentDB) will show as not applicable because deletion protection is set at the cluster level. Identifier: RDS_INSTANCE_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED Resource Types: AWS::RDS::DBInstance Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: databaseEngines (Optional

Warning Some RDS DB instances within a Cluster (Aurora/DocumentDB) will show as not applicable because deletion protection is set at the cluster level. RDS_INSTANCE_DELETION_PROTECTION_ENABLED.title: Rds Instance Deletion Protection Enabled

RDS_INSTANCE_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB instances on supported engines (mysql, postgres, aurora, aurora-mysql, aurora-postgresql) whose IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled is false.
RDS_INSTANCE_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) instance has AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an Amazon RDS instance does not have IAM authentication enabled.
RDS_INSTANCE_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable IAM database authentication on supported RDS engines via aws rds modify-db-instance --enable-iam-database-authentication --apply-immediately, or Terraform aws_db_instance.iam_database_authentication_enabled = true. Update clients to fetch short-lived tokens with rds-db:connect IAM permissions.
RDS_INSTANCE_IAM_AUTHENTICATION_ENABLED.title: RDS DB instances must enable IAM database authentication

RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB instance whose PubliclyAccessible flag is true (DNS resolves to a public IP).
RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) instances are not publicly accessible. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the publiclyAccessible field is true in the instance configuration item.
RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Set PubliclyAccessible=false on each RDS instance via aws rds modify-db-instance --no-publicly-accessible --apply-immediately or Terraform aws_db_instance.publicly_accessible = false. Place instances in private subnets and provide access via VPN, AWS PrivateLink, or bastion hosts.
RDS_INSTANCE_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.title: RDS DB instances must not be publicly accessible

RDS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any Amazon RDS DB instance not selected for backup by an active AWS Backup plan. (Aurora DB clusters are out of scope.)
RDS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: rds_db_instance.engine NOT IN ['aurora','aurora-mysql','aurora-postgresql'] AND rds_db_instance.arn IN aws_backup_plan.selections.resources
RDS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) databases are present in AWS Backup plans. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Amazon RDS databases are not included in any AWS Backup plan.
RDS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the RDS DB instance to an AWS Backup plan via tag- or ARN-based resource selection (aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection.resources) so AWS Backup creates and retains snapshots in a Backup Vault.
RDS_IN_BACKUP_PLAN.title: RDS DB instances must be included in an AWS Backup plan

RDS_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB instances in available/backing-up/storage-optimization/storage-full status whose EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports does not include the engine-specific required log types (e.g. error/general/slowquery for MySQL, postgresql/upgrade for Postgres) or those listed in additionalLogs.
RDS_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: rds_db_instance.Status in ['available','backing-up','storage-optimization','storage-full'] AND every t in required_log_types(engine) : t in rds_db_instance.EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports
RDS_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if respective logs of Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) are enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any log types are not enabled.
RDS_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable engine-appropriate log exports on each RDS instance (e.g. error, general, slowquery for MySQL; postgresql and upgrade for PostgreSQL). Use aws rds modify-db-instance --cloudwatch-logs-export-configuration EnableLogTypes=... or Terraform aws_db_instance.enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports. Configure parameter groups to actually emit the logs (e.g. general_log = 1).
RDS_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: RDS DB instance database logs must be enabled

RDS_MULTI_AZ_SUPPORT.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails RDS DB instances whose MultiAZ flag is false. Aurora, DocumentDB, and Neptune DB instances are out of scope.
RDS_MULTI_AZ_SUPPORT.condition_logic: rds_db_instance.MultiAZ == true AND rds_db_instance.Engine NOT IN ['aurora','aurora-mysql','aurora-postgresql','docdb','neptune']
RDS_MULTI_AZ_SUPPORT.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether high availability is enabled for your RDS DB instances. In a Multi-AZ deployment, Amazon RDS automatically provisions and maintains a synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone.
RDS_MULTI_AZ_SUPPORT.remediation_summary: Enable Multi-AZ on each RDS DB instance via aws rds modify-db-instance --multi-az --apply-immediately, or Terraform aws_db_instance.multi_az = true. The change provisions a synchronous standby in another AZ during the next maintenance window.
RDS_MULTI_AZ_SUPPORT.title: RDS DB instances must use Multi-AZ deployments

RDS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that verifies each RDS DB instance (optionally filtered by tags or resourceId) is included in an active AWS Backup plan, with optional retention bounds and Backup Vault Lock checks.
RDS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: rds_db_instance IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
RDS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) instances are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon RDS Database instance is not covered by a backup plan.
RDS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the RDS DB instance to an AWS Backup plan with a tag-based or resource-based selection. Use aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection / aws_backup_plan, and configure a Backup Vault Lock if retention guarantees are required.
RDS_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: RDS DB instances must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB snapshot or DB cluster snapshot whose restore attribute is shared with 'all' (publicly accessible).
RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) snapshots are public. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any existing and new Amazon RDS snapshots are public.
RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Remove the public sharing from each affected snapshot via aws rds modify-db-snapshot-attribute --attribute-name restore --values-to-remove all (or aws rds modify-db-cluster-snapshot-attribute), or Terraform aws_db_snapshot. Audit IaC pipelines that may set shared_accounts = ["all"].
RDS_SNAPSHOTS_PUBLIC_PROHIBITED.title: RDS snapshots must not be public

RDS_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB or DB cluster snapshot whose Encrypted attribute is false.
RDS_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) DB snapshots are encrypted. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon RDS DB snapshots are not encrypted.
RDS_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Replace unencrypted RDS DB and DB cluster snapshots with encrypted copies: use aws rds copy-db-snapshot / copy-db-cluster-snapshot --kms-key-id <kms-arn> to produce an encrypted copy, then delete the original. Going forward, ensure source DB instances/clusters have storage encryption enabled so future snapshots are automatically encrypted.
RDS_SNAPSHOT_ENCRYPTED.title: RDS DB and cluster snapshots must be encrypted

RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any RDS DB instance whose StorageEncrypted attribute is false, optionally requiring a specific KMS key id/arn.
RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED.condition_logic: rds_db_instance.StorageEncrypted == true AND (kmsKeyId == null OR rds_db_instance.KmsKeyId == kmsKeyId)
RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if storage encryption is enabled for your Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) DB instances. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if storage encryption is not enabled.
RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED.remediation_summary: Recreate unencrypted RDS DB instances with encryption enabled: snapshot the source, copy the snapshot with --kms-key-id, restore as a new encrypted DB instance, and switch traffic over before deleting the unencrypted instance. For new instances, set StorageEncrypted = true (and KmsKeyId) via aws rds create-db-instance or Terraform aws_db_instance.storage_encrypted = true / kms_key_id = ....
RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED.title: RDS DB instances must have storage encryption enabled

Identifier: REDSHIFT_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED Resource Types: AWS::Redshift::Cluster Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), China (Beijing), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Middle East (UAE), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbou
REDSHIFT_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift clusters are logging audits to a specific bucket. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if audit logging is not enabled for a Redshift cluster or if the 'bucketNames' parameter is provided but the audit logging destination does not match. Identifier: REDSHIFT_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED Resource Types: AWS::Redshift::Cluster Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), China (Beijing), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Middle East (UAE), Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Melbou

REDSHIFT_AUDIT_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: Redshift Audit Logging Enabled

REDSHIFT_BACKUP_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a Redshift cluster whose AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is 0 or outside the inclusive range [MinRetentionPeriod, MaxRetentionPeriod].
REDSHIFT_BACKUP_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks that Amazon Redshift automated snapshots are enabled for clusters. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the value for automatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is greater than MaxRetentionPeriod or less than MinRetentionPeriod or the value is 0.
REDSHIFT_BACKUP_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure Amazon Redshift clusters to retain automated snapshots within the required range using aws redshift modify-cluster --automated-snapshot-retention-period <days>, or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster.automated_snapshot_retention_period (1-35).
REDSHIFT_BACKUP_ENABLED.title: Redshift clusters must have automated snapshots with the configured retention

REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_CONFIGURATION_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters whose Encrypted, LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled, or NodeType do not match the configured loggingEnabled / clusterDbEncrypted / nodeTypes parameters.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_CONFIGURATION_CHECK.condition_logic: redshift_cluster.Encrypted == clusterDbEncrypted AND redshift_cluster.LoggingStatus.LoggingEnabled == loggingEnabled AND (nodeTypes == null OR redshift_cluster.NodeType in nodeTypes)
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_CONFIGURATION_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift clusters have the specified settings. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon Redshift cluster is not encrypted or encrypted with another key, or if a cluster does not have audit logging enabled.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_CONFIGURATION_CHECK.remediation_summary: Enable encryption-at-rest, audit logging, and use approved node types on each Redshift cluster. Apply via aws redshift modify-cluster --encrypted --kms-key-id ..., aws redshift enable-logging --bucket-name ..., aws redshift modify-cluster --node-type ..., or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster (encrypted, logging, node_type).
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_CONFIGURATION_CHECK.title: Redshift clusters must enable encryption, audit logging, and approved node types

REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_KMS_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters that are unencrypted, or whose KmsKeyId is not in the kmsKeyArns list when supplied.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_KMS_ENABLED.condition_logic: redshift_cluster.Encrypted == true AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR redshift_cluster.KmsKeyId in kmsKeyArns)
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_KMS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift clusters are using a specified AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for encryption. The rule is COMPLIANT if encryption is enabled and the cluster is encrypted with the key provided in the kmsKeyArn parameter. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the cluster is not encrypted or encrypted with another key.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_KMS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable encryption with an approved KMS key on each Redshift cluster via aws redshift modify-cluster --encrypted --kms-key-id <arn>, or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster.encrypted = true and kms_key_id = <arn>. Snapshot the cluster first; the resize operation may take significant time on large clusters.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_KMS_ENABLED.title: Redshift clusters must be encrypted with the approved KMS keys

REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_MAINTENANCESETTINGS_CHE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters whose AllowVersionUpgrade differs from allowVersionUpgrade, whose PreferredMaintenanceWindow does not match preferredMaintenanceWindow (when set), or whose AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod is below automatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_MAINTENANCESETTINGS_CHE.condition_logic: redshift_cluster.AllowVersionUpgrade == allowVersionUpgrade AND (preferredMaintenanceWindow == null OR redshift_cluster.PreferredMaintenanceWindow == preferredMaintenanceWindow) AND redshift_cluster.AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod >= automatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_MAINTENANCESETTINGS_CHE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift clusters have the specified maintenance settings. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the automatic upgrades to major version is disabled.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_MAINTENANCESETTINGS_CHE.remediation_summary: Update each Redshift cluster's maintenance settings: enable AllowVersionUpgrade, set the PreferredMaintenanceWindow, and configure AutomatedSnapshotRetentionPeriod (>=1). Apply via aws redshift modify-cluster --allow-version-upgrade --preferred-maintenance-window ... --automated-snapshot-retention-period ..., or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster fields.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_MAINTENANCESETTINGS_CHE.title: Redshift clusters must have approved maintenance and snapshot settings

REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters whose PubliclyAccessible flag is true.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether Amazon Redshift clusters are not publicly accessible. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the publiclyAccessible field is true in the cluster configuration item.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.remediation_summary: Set PubliclyAccessible=false on each Redshift cluster via aws redshift modify-cluster --no-publicly-accessible, or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster.publicly_accessible = false. Place clusters in private subnets and use VPN/PrivateLink/SSH bastion or aws_redshift_endpoint_access for client access.
REDSHIFT_CLUSTER_PUBLIC_ACCESS_CHECK.title: Redshift clusters must not be publicly accessible

The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the admin username for a Redshift cluster is set to “awsuser” or if the username does not match what is listed in parameter. REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_ADMIN_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Redshift cluster has changed the admin username from its default value.
