REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_ADMIN_CHECK.title: Redshift Default Admin Check

REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if a Redshift cluster has changed its database name from the default value. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the database name for a Redshift cluster is set to “dev”, or if the optional parameter is provided and the database name does not match. Identifier: REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Redshift::Cluster Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Ca
REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a Redshift cluster has changed its database name from the default value. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the database name for a Redshift cluster is set to “dev”, or if the optional parameter is provided and the database name does not match. Identifier: REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::Redshift::Cluster Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions except Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Thailand), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), AWS GovCloud (US-East), AWS GovCloud (US-West), Mexico (Central), Israel (Tel Aviv), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Ca
REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
REDSHIFT_DEFAULT_DB_NAME_CHECK.title: Redshift Default Db Name Check

REDSHIFT_ENHANCED_VPC_ROUTING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters whose EnhancedVpcRouting flag is false, meaning COPY/UNLOAD traffic can flow over the public internet.
REDSHIFT_ENHANCED_VPC_ROUTING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift cluster has 'enhancedVpcRouting' enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'enhancedVpcRouting' is not enabled or if the configuration.enhancedVpcRouting field is 'false'.
REDSHIFT_ENHANCED_VPC_ROUTING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable enhanced VPC routing on each Redshift cluster via aws redshift modify-cluster --enhanced-vpc-routing or Terraform aws_redshift_cluster.enhanced_vpc_routing = true. Ensure the VPC has the required S3 / KMS / etc. endpoints so COPY/UNLOAD traffic remains within AWS network.
REDSHIFT_ENHANCED_VPC_ROUTING_ENABLED.title: Redshift clusters must enable enhanced VPC routing

REDSHIFT_REQUIRE_TLS_SSL.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Redshift clusters whose attached parameter group does not set require_ssl = true.
REDSHIFT_REQUIRE_TLS_SSL.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Redshift clusters require TLS/SSL encryption to connect to SQL clients. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any Amazon Redshift cluster has parameter require_SSL not set to true.
REDSHIFT_REQUIRE_TLS_SSL.remediation_summary: Set require_ssl = true on the cluster parameter group attached to each Redshift cluster via aws redshift modify-cluster-parameter-group --parameters ParameterName=require_ssl,ParameterValue=true,ApplyType=static, or Terraform aws_redshift_parameter_group.parameter { name = "require_ssl", value = "true" }. Reboot the cluster to apply.
REDSHIFT_REQUIRE_TLS_SSL.title: Redshift clusters must require TLS/SSL for SQL client connections

RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS.condition_description: Configuration-change/periodic rule that fails any security group with an inbound TCP rule whose source CIDR covers all addresses (0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0) and whose port range includes any of blockedPort1..5 or any port in blockedPorts.
RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS.condition_logic: FOR rule IN security_group.IpPermissions WHERE rule.IpProtocol == 'tcp' AND ('0.0.0.0/0' IN rule.IpRanges OR '::/0' IN rule.Ipv6Ranges): NOT EXISTS port IN union(blockedPorts, [blockedPort1, blockedPort2, blockedPort3, blockedPort4, blockedPort5]) WHERE rule.FromPort <= port <= rule.ToPort
RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the security groups in use do not allow unrestricted incoming Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) traffic to specified ports. The rule is COMPLIANT if Port access is blocked to all TCP traffic, or open to TCP traffic through Inbound rules where the source is a single IPv4/IPv6 address or a CIDR range that does not cover all addresses. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if IP addresses for inbound TCP connections are not restricted to specified ports.
RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS.remediation_summary: Remove inbound rules on security groups that allow 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to the blocked TCP ports (20, 21, 3306, 3389, 4333 by default, plus anything in blockedPorts). Restrict the source to specific corporate, bastion, or load-balancer CIDRs/security groups via aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress / authorize-security-group-ingress, or Terraform aws_security_group_rule / aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule.
RESTRICTED_COMMON_PORTS.title: Security groups must not allow unrestricted ingress to common high-risk ports

RESTRICTED_SSH.condition_description: Configuration-change/periodic rule that fails a security group with any inbound rule for TCP 22 whose source CIDR is 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
RESTRICTED_SSH.condition_logic: FOR rule IN security_group.IpPermissions WHERE rule.IpProtocol == 'tcp' AND rule.FromPort <= 22 <= rule.ToPort: '0.0.0.0/0' NOT IN rule.IpRanges AND '::/0' NOT IN rule.Ipv6Ranges
RESTRICTED_SSH.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the incoming SSH traffic for the security groups is accessible. The rule is COMPLIANT if the IP addresses of the incoming SSH traffic in the security groups are restricted (CIDR other than 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0). Otherwise, NON_COMPLIANT.
RESTRICTED_SSH.remediation_summary: Remove or scope-down inbound rules on security groups that allow 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to TCP 22. Restrict SSH ingress to specific bastion, VPN, or corporate CIDR ranges (or use Systems Manager Session Manager instead) via aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress + authorize-security-group-ingress, or Terraform aws_security_group_rule / aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule with cidr_blocks/source_security_group_id.
RESTRICTED_SSH.title: Security groups must not allow unrestricted SSH ingress

ROOT_ACCOUNT_HARDWARE_MFA_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if root user MFA is not enrolled with a hardware device. Accounts without root credentials are NOT_APPLICABLE.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_HARDWARE_MFA_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your AWS account is enabled to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) hardware device to sign in with root credentials. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any virtual MFA devices are permitted for signing in with root credentials.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_HARDWARE_MFA_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enroll a hardware MFA device for the AWS root user. From the root sign-in, navigate to IAM > My security credentials > Multi-factor authentication, deactivate any virtual MFA, then activate a U2F/FIDO security key or hardware TOTP token. Hardware MFA cannot be set via API; perform this manually and document the recovery process.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_HARDWARE_MFA_ENABLED.title: Root user must have hardware MFA enabled

ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that calls IAM GetAccountSummary and fails the account if the root user does not have an MFA device enabled. Returns NOT_APPLICABLE when the account has no root user credentials.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the root user of your AWS account requires multi-factor authentication for console sign-in. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) root account user does not have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Sign in as the root user, go to My Security Credentials, and enable a virtual or hardware MFA device for the root user (FIDO security key recommended). Lock the device away after enabling and use IAM users / IAM Identity Center for daily access.
ROOT_ACCOUNT_MFA_ENABLED.title: Root user must have MFA enabled

S3_ACCESS_POINT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 access point (excluding those listed in excludedAccessPoints) whose PublicAccessBlockConfiguration does not have all four block-public-access flags set to true.
S3_ACCESS_POINT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.condition_logic: access_point.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicAcls == true AND access_point.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.IgnorePublicAcls == true AND access_point.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicPolicy == true AND access_point.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.RestrictPublicBuckets == true OR access_point.Name in excludedAccessPoints
S3_ACCESS_POINT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon S3 access points have block public access settings enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if block public access settings are not enabled for S3 access points.
S3_ACCESS_POINT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.remediation_summary: Enable all four Block Public Access settings on each S3 access point via aws s3control put-access-point-public-access-block --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true, or define them at create time in Terraform aws_s3_access_point.public_access_block_configuration.
S3_ACCESS_POINT_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.title: S3 access points must enable Block Public Access settings

S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails the account if the AccountPublicAccessBlock does not match the four boolean parameters BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets (all default True).
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.condition_logic: account_public_access_block.BlockPublicAcls == BlockPublicAcls AND account_public_access_block.IgnorePublicAcls == IgnorePublicAcls AND account_public_access_block.BlockPublicPolicy == BlockPublicPolicy AND account_public_access_block.RestrictPublicBuckets == RestrictPublicBuckets
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the required public access block settings are configured from account level. The rule is only NON_COMPLIANT when the fields set below do not match the corresponding fields in the configuration item.
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.remediation_summary: Enable account-level Block Public Access via aws s3control put-public-access-block --account-id <id> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true, or Terraform aws_s3_account_public_access_block resource. Apply this from a security-tooling account or via AWS Organizations service control policy.
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS.title: S3 account-level Block Public Access settings must be enabled

S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS_PE.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if any of the four S3 Block Public Access settings (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) is not set to true (or to the value supplied via parameters).
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS_PE.condition_logic: s3_account_block.BlockPublicAcls == BlockPublicAcls AND s3_account_block.IgnorePublicAcls == IgnorePublicAcls AND s3_account_block.BlockPublicPolicy == BlockPublicPolicy AND s3_account_block.RestrictPublicBuckets == RestrictPublicBuckets
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS_PE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the required public access block settings are configured at the account level. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the configuration item does not match one or more settings from parameters (or default).
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS_PE.remediation_summary: Enable all four S3 Block Public Access settings at the account level using aws s3control put-public-access-block --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true, or Terraform aws_s3_account_public_access_block with all four flags set to true.
S3_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_BLOCKS_PE.title: Account-level S3 Block Public Access settings must all be enabled

S3_BUCKET_ACL_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket whose ACL contains a Grant whose Grantee is a user (CanonicalUser, AmazonCustomerByEmail, or Group AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers) other than the bucket owner.
S3_BUCKET_ACL_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: NOT exists(grant in s3_bucket.AccessControlList.Grants where grant.Grantee.Type in ['CanonicalUser','AmazonCustomerByEmail','Group'] AND grant.Grantee.ID != bucket.Owner.ID)
S3_BUCKET_ACL_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) Buckets allow user permissions through access control lists (ACLs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if ACLs are configured for user access in Amazon S3 Buckets.
S3_BUCKET_ACL_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Adopt bucket-owner-enforced object ownership and remove ACL grants from each S3 bucket. Use aws s3api put-bucket-ownership-controls --ownership BucketOwnerEnforced and aws s3api put-bucket-acl --acl private, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_ownership_controls and aws_s3_bucket_acl set to private. Manage access via bucket policies and IAM instead.
S3_BUCKET_ACL_PROHIBITED.title: S3 buckets must not use ACL-based user permissions

S3_BUCKET_BLACKLISTED_ACTIONS_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an S3 bucket if its policy contains an Allow statement whose Action matches blacklistedActionPattern and whose Principal is from another AWS account.
S3_BUCKET_BLACKLISTED_ACTIONS_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: NOT exists(stmt in s3_bucket.Policy.Statement where stmt.Effect == 'Allow' AND stmt.Action matches blacklistedActionPattern AND stmt.Principal.AccountId != bucket.OwnerAccountId)
S3_BUCKET_BLACKLISTED_ACTIONS_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket policy does not allow blocklisted bucket-level and object-level actions on resources in the bucket for principals from other AWS accounts. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any blocklisted actions are allowed by the Amazon S3 bucket policy.
S3_BUCKET_BLACKLISTED_ACTIONS_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Tighten S3 bucket policies so other AWS accounts cannot perform blocklisted actions (e.g., s3:GetBucket*, s3:DeleteObject). Update aws s3api put-bucket-policy or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_policy with explicit Principal lists and Resource scoping, and use aws:PrincipalOrgID conditions to restrict cross-account access to your AWS Organization.
S3_BUCKET_BLACKLISTED_ACTIONS_PROHIBITED.title: S3 bucket policies must not allow blocked cross-account actions

S3_BUCKET_DEFAULT_LOCK_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an S3 bucket whose ObjectLockConfiguration.ObjectLockEnabled is not Enabled, or whose default Rule.DefaultRetention.Mode does not match the optional mode parameter (GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE).
S3_BUCKET_DEFAULT_LOCK_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the S3 bucket has lock enabled, by default. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the lock is not enabled.
S3_BUCKET_DEFAULT_LOCK_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable S3 Object Lock at bucket creation time and configure a default retention rule (GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE mode for the required number of days/years) using aws s3api put-object-lock-configuration, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket.object_lock_enabled = true plus aws_s3_bucket_object_lock_configuration.rule.default_retention. Note that Object Lock cannot be enabled on existing buckets without re-creation.
S3_BUCKET_DEFAULT_LOCK_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must have Object Lock enabled by default

S3_BUCKET_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket (other than those in excludedPublicBuckets) whose bucket-level Block Public Access settings are not all true.
S3_BUCKET_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: (s3_bucket.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicAcls AND s3_bucket.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.IgnorePublicAcls AND s3_bucket.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicPolicy AND s3_bucket.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.RestrictPublicBuckets) OR s3_bucket.Name in excludedPublicBuckets
S3_BUCKET_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if S3 buckets are publicly accessible. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an S3 bucket is not listed in the excludedPublicBuckets parameter and bucket level settings are public.
S3_BUCKET_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Enable bucket-level Block Public Access on each S3 bucket via aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket <name> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. Add genuinely public buckets (e.g., for static sites) to the excludedPublicBuckets allow list.
S3_BUCKET_LEVEL_PUBLIC_ACCESS_PROHIBITED.title: S3 bucket-level public access must be blocked

S3_BUCKET_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an S3 bucket whose LoggingConfiguration is empty, optionally requiring the destination bucket to equal targetBucket and the prefix to equal targetPrefix.
S3_BUCKET_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: s3_bucket.LoggingConfiguration.DestinationBucketName != null AND (targetBucket == null OR s3_bucket.LoggingConfiguration.DestinationBucketName == targetBucket) AND (targetPrefix == null OR s3_bucket.LoggingConfiguration.LogFilePrefix == targetPrefix)
S3_BUCKET_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if logging is enabled for your S3 buckets. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if logging is not enabled.
S3_BUCKET_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable S3 server access logging on each bucket, pointing at a dedicated log-archive bucket and an optional prefix. Apply via aws s3api put-bucket-logging or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_logging.target_bucket / target_prefix; ensure the destination bucket has the required AWS Logs Delivery permissions.
S3_BUCKET_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must have server access logging enabled

S3_BUCKET_MFA_DELETE_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket whose VersioningConfiguration.MFADelete is not 'Enabled'.
S3_BUCKET_MFA_DELETE_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if MFA Delete is enabled in the Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket versioning configuration. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if MFA Delete is not enabled.
S3_BUCKET_MFA_DELETE_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable MFA Delete on each versioned S3 bucket. From the AWS root credentials only, run aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket <name> --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled,MFADelete=Enabled --mfa "<serial> <token>". MFA Delete cannot currently be enabled with Terraform; manage it via a one-time root operation and document the recovery procedure.
S3_BUCKET_MFA_DELETE_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must enable MFA Delete on versioning

S3_BUCKET_POLICY_GRANTEE_CHECK.condition_description: Checks that the access granted by the Amazon S3 bucket is restricted by any of the AWS principals, federated users, service principals, IP addresses, or VPCs that you provide. The rule is COMPLIANT if a bucket policy is not present. For example, if the input parameter to the rule is the list of two principals: 111122223333 and 444455556666 and the bucket policy specifies that only 111122223333 can access the bucket, then the rule is COMPLIANT. With the same input parameters: If the bucket policy specifies that 111122223333 and 444455556666 can access the bucket, it is also COMPLIANT. However,
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_GRANTEE_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks that the access granted by the Amazon S3 bucket is restricted by any of the AWS principals, federated users, service principals, IP addresses, or VPCs that you provide. The rule is COMPLIANT if a bucket policy is not present. For example, if the input parameter to the rule is the list of two principals: 111122223333 and 444455556666 and the bucket policy specifies that only 111122223333 can access the bucket, then the rule is COMPLIANT. With the same input parameters: If the bucket policy specifies that 111122223333 and 444455556666 can access the bucket, it is also COMPLIANT. However,
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_GRANTEE_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule S3_BUCKET_POLICY_GRANTEE_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_GRANTEE_CHECK.title: S3 Bucket Policy Grantee Check

S3_BUCKET_POLICY_NOT_MORE_PERMISSIVE.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an S3 bucket whose effective bucket policy grants permissions beyond those allowed by the controlPolicy parameter (a reference policy that defines an upper bound on inter-account access).
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_NOT_MORE_PERMISSIVE.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon Simple Storage Service bucket policies do not allow other inter-account permissions than the control Amazon S3 bucket policy that you provide.
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_NOT_MORE_PERMISSIVE.remediation_summary: Tighten the S3 bucket policy so it does not allow actions beyond the approved control policy. Update via aws s3api put-bucket-policy or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_policy and ensure cross-account access uses the same actions/resources/conditions defined in the control policy. Consider a service control policy that enforces this baseline organization-wide.
S3_BUCKET_POLICY_NOT_MORE_PERMISSIVE.title: S3 bucket policies must not exceed an approved control policy

S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change/periodic rule that evaluates each S3 bucket's Block Public Access settings, bucket policy, and ACL. A bucket is NON_COMPLIANT if BPA does not restrict public policies AND the policy grants public read access, or if BPA does not restrict public ACLs AND the ACL grants public read access.
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: (bucket.PublicAccessBlock.RestrictPublicPolicy == true OR NOT policy_allows_public_read(bucket.Policy)) AND (bucket.PublicAccessBlock.IgnorePublicAcls == true OR NOT acl_allows_public_read(bucket.ACL))
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon S3 buckets do not allow public read access. The rule checks the Block Public Access settings, the bucket policy, and the bucket access control list (ACL). The rule is compliant when both the Block Public Access setting restricts public policies (or the bucket policy does not allow public read access) and the Block Public Access setting restricts public ACLs (or the bucket ACL does not allow public read access).
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Enable bucket-level S3 Block Public Access (BlockPublicPolicy = true and IgnorePublicAcls = true), and remove any policy or ACL grant of s3:GetObject / Read access to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers. Use aws s3api put-public-access-block, aws s3api put-bucket-policy / delete-bucket-policy, and aws s3api put-bucket-acl, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, aws_s3_bucket_policy, and aws_s3_bucket_acl.
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED.title: S3 buckets must prohibit public read access

S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED.condition_description: Configuration-change/periodic rule that evaluates each S3 bucket's Block Public Access settings, bucket policy, and ACL. A bucket is NON_COMPLIANT if BPA does not restrict public policies AND the policy grants public write access, or if BPA does not restrict public ACLs AND the ACL grants public write access.
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED.condition_logic: (bucket.PublicAccessBlock.RestrictPublicPolicy == true OR NOT policy_allows_public_write(bucket.Policy)) AND (bucket.PublicAccessBlock.IgnorePublicAcls == true OR NOT acl_allows_public_write(bucket.ACL))
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon S3 buckets do not allow public write access. The rule checks the Block Public Access settings, the bucket policy, and the bucket access control list (ACL). The rule is compliant when both the Block Public Access setting restricts public policies (or the bucket policy does not allow public write access) and the Block Public Access setting restricts public ACLs (or the bucket ACL does not allow public write access).
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED.remediation_summary: Enable bucket-level S3 Block Public Access (BlockPublicPolicy = true and IgnorePublicAcls = true), then remove any policy or ACL grant that allows s3:PutObject / Write / WriteAcp / FullControl to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers. Apply via aws s3api put-public-access-block, aws s3api put-bucket-policy, aws s3api put-bucket-acl, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block + aws_s3_bucket_policy + aws_s3_bucket_acl.
S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED.title: S3 buckets must prohibit public write access

S3_BUCKET_REPLICATION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails S3 buckets without an enabled ReplicationConfiguration rule. When ReplicationType is supplied, only the matching variant ('CROSS-REGION' or 'SAME-REGION') is required.
S3_BUCKET_REPLICATION_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(rule in s3_bucket.ReplicationConfiguration.Rules where rule.Status == 'Enabled') AND (ReplicationType == null OR rule.replication_type == ReplicationType)
S3_BUCKET_REPLICATION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if S3 buckets have replication rules enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an S3 bucket does not have a replication rule or has a replication rule that is not enabled.
S3_BUCKET_REPLICATION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure cross-region or same-region replication on each S3 bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-replication, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_replication_configuration with at least one rule { status = "Enabled", destination { bucket = ... } } and an IAM role granting s3:Replicate*/s3:GetObject permissions.
S3_BUCKET_REPLICATION_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must enable replication

S3_BUCKET_SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket without a default ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration (AES256 / aws:kms / aws:kms:dsse) and without a bucket policy that explicitly denies unencrypted PutObject requests.
S3_BUCKET_SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(rule in s3_bucket.ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration.Rules where rule.ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm in ['AES256','aws:kms','aws:kms:dsse']) OR s3_bucket.Policy denies PutObject WHEN s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing
S3_BUCKET_SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if your Amazon S3 bucket either has the Amazon S3 default encryption enabled or that the Amazon S3 bucket policy explicitly denies put-object requests without server side encryption that uses AES-256 or AWS Key Management Service. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if your Amazon S3 bucket is not encrypted by default.
S3_BUCKET_SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable default encryption on each S3 bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-encryption with an SSE-S3 (AES256) or SSE-KMS rule, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration. Optionally add a bucket policy that denies s3:PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is missing as a defense-in-depth control.
S3_BUCKET_SERVER_SIDE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must enable server-side encryption by default

S3_BUCKET_SSL_REQUESTS_ONLY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket whose bucket policy does not contain a Deny statement on s3:* with the condition aws:SecureTransport=false.
S3_BUCKET_SSL_REQUESTS_ONLY.condition_logic: exists(stmt in s3_bucket.Policy.Statement where stmt.Effect == 'Deny' AND stmt.Action contains 's3:*' AND stmt.Condition['Bool']['aws:SecureTransport'] == 'false')
S3_BUCKET_SSL_REQUESTS_ONLY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if S3 buckets have policies that require requests to use SSL/TLS. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if any S3 bucket has policies allowing HTTP requests.
S3_BUCKET_SSL_REQUESTS_ONLY.remediation_summary: Attach a bucket policy that denies s3:* on the bucket and its objects when aws:SecureTransport is false. Apply via aws s3api put-bucket-policy or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_policy with a statement { Effect = "Deny", Action = "s3:*", Condition = { Bool = { "aws:SecureTransport" = "false" } } }.
S3_BUCKET_SSL_REQUESTS_ONLY.title: S3 bucket policies must require SSL/TLS requests only

S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket whose VersioningConfiguration.Status is not Enabled, and optionally fails buckets whose MFADelete status does not match isMfaDeleteEnabled.
S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if versioning is enabled for your S3 buckets. Optionally, the rule checks if MFA delete is enabled for your S3 buckets.
S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable versioning on each S3 bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled (and optionally MFADelete=Enabled while signed in as root), or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_versioning.versioning_configuration.status = "Enabled". Combine with lifecycle policies to manage noncurrent version costs.
S3_BUCKET_VERSIONING_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must have versioning enabled

S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KMS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket whose default encryption SSEAlgorithm is not aws:kms / aws:kms:dsse, or whose KMSMasterKeyID is not in kmsKeyArns when supplied.
S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KMS.condition_logic: exists(rule in s3_bucket.ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration.Rules where rule.ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm in ['aws:kms','aws:kms:dsse'] AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR rule.ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.KMSMasterKeyID in kmsKeyArns))
S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KMS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the S3 buckets are encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the S3 bucket is not encrypted with an AWS KMS key.
S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KMS.remediation_summary: Configure default encryption with an AWS KMS key on each S3 bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-encryption with ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault.SSEAlgorithm=aws:kms,KMSMasterKeyID=<arn>, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration with sse_algorithm = "aws:kms" and kms_master_key_id pointing at the approved key.
S3_DEFAULT_ENCRYPTION_KMS.title: S3 buckets must default-encrypt objects with AWS KMS

S3_EVENT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any S3 bucket without a NotificationConfiguration. When destinationArn or eventTypes are set, the bucket's notifications must include the configured destination ARN and cover all the requested event types.
S3_EVENT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.condition_logic: len(s3_bucket.NotificationConfiguration) > 0 AND (destinationArn == null OR exists(notif where notif.DestinationArn == destinationArn)) AND (eventTypes == null OR every t in eventTypes : t in s3_bucket.NotificationConfiguration.events)
S3_EVENT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon S3 Events Notifications are enabled on an S3 bucket. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if S3 Events Notifications are not set on a bucket, or if the event type or destination do not match the eventTypes and destinationArn parameters.
S3_EVENT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Configure S3 event notifications on each bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_notification with topic/queue/lambda configurations and the required events (e.g. s3:ObjectCreated:*, s3:ObjectRemoved:*) routing to a security-monitored SNS topic, SQS queue, or Lambda.
S3_EVENT_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED.title: S3 buckets must enable event notifications

S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if a lifecycle rule is configured for an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there is no active lifecycle configuration rules or the configuration does not match with the parameter values. Identifier: S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::S3::Bucket Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: targetTransitionDays (Optional) Type: int Number of days after object creation when objects are transitioned to a specified storage class (for example, 30 days). targetExpirationDays (Optional) Type: int N
S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a lifecycle rule is configured for an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there is no active lifecycle configuration rules or the configuration does not match with the parameter values. Identifier: S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::S3::Bucket Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: targetTransitionDays (Optional) Type: int Number of days after object creation when objects are transitioned to a specified storage class (for example, 30 days). targetExpirationDays (Optional) Type: int N
S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
S3_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.title: S3 Lifecycle Policy Check

S3_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_description: Periodic rule that verifies each S3 bucket (optionally filtered by tags or resourceId) is included in an active AWS Backup plan, with optional retention bounds and Backup Vault Lock checks.
S3_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.condition_logic: s3_bucket IN aws_backup_plan.resource_assignments AND (backupVaultLockCheck != 'True' OR vault.lock.retention_days BETWEEN minRetentionDays AND maxRetentionDays)
S3_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) buckets are protected by a backup plan. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Amazon S3 bucket is not covered by a backup plan.
S3_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.remediation_summary: Add the S3 bucket to an AWS Backup plan with a tag-based or resource-based selection. Use aws backup create-backup-selection or Terraform aws_backup_selection / aws_backup_plan and configure a Backup Vault Lock when retention guarantees are required. Replication and versioning are not substitutes for Backup-based snapshots.
S3_RESOURCES_PROTECTED_BY_BACKUP_PLAN.title: S3 buckets must be protected by an AWS Backup plan

S3_VERSION_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any version-enabled S3 bucket (or any bucket listed in bucketNames) whose LifecycleConfiguration does not contain at least one enabled rule.
S3_VERSION_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.condition_logic: (s3_bucket.VersioningConfiguration.Status != 'Enabled' AND s3_bucket.Name NOT IN bucketNames) OR exists(rule in s3_bucket.LifecycleConfiguration.Rules where rule.Status == 'Enabled')
S3_VERSION_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) version enabled buckets have lifecycle policy configured. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Amazon S3 lifecycle policy is not enabled.
S3_VERSION_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.remediation_summary: Add a lifecycle policy to each versioned S3 bucket via aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration, or Terraform aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration with rules for noncurrent_version_transition and noncurrent_version_expiration to control storage costs while retaining object history.
S3_VERSION_LIFECYCLE_POLICY_CHECK.title: Versioned S3 buckets must configure a lifecycle policy

SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails SageMaker endpoint configurations whose KmsKeyId is not set, or whose KmsKeyId is not in kmsKeyArns when supplied.
SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY.condition_logic: sagemaker_endpoint_config.KmsKeyId != null AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR sagemaker_endpoint_config.KmsKeyId in kmsKeyArns)
SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key is configured for an Amazon SageMaker endpoint configuration. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'KmsKeyId' is not specified for the Amazon SageMaker endpoint configuration.
SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY.remediation_summary: Recreate each SageMaker endpoint configuration with KmsKeyId set to an approved customer-managed KMS key. Use aws sagemaker create-endpoint-config --kms-key-id <arn> followed by aws sagemaker update-endpoint, or Terraform aws_sagemaker_endpoint_configuration.kms_key_arn.
SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY.title: SageMaker endpoint configurations must use a KMS key

SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_KMS_KEY_CONF.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails SageMaker notebook instances whose KmsKeyId is null, or whose KmsKeyId is not in kmsKeyArns when supplied.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_KMS_KEY_CONF.condition_logic: sagemaker_notebook_instance.KmsKeyId != null AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR sagemaker_notebook_instance.KmsKeyId in kmsKeyArns)
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_KMS_KEY_CONF.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key is configured for an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if 'KmsKeyId' is not specified for the SageMaker notebook instance.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_KMS_KEY_CONF.remediation_summary: Recreate each SageMaker notebook instance with KmsKeyId set to an approved customer-managed KMS key (this property cannot be changed in place). Use aws sagemaker create-notebook-instance --kms-key-id <arn>, or Terraform aws_sagemaker_notebook_instance.kms_key_id.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_INSTANCE_KMS_KEY_CONF.title: SageMaker notebook instances must use a KMS key for storage encryption

SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_NO_DIRECT_INTERNET_AC.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails SageMaker notebook instances whose DirectInternetAccess setting is 'Enabled'.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_NO_DIRECT_INTERNET_AC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if direct internet access is disabled for an Amazon SageMaker notebook instance. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a SageMaker notebook instance is internet-enabled.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_NO_DIRECT_INTERNET_AC.remediation_summary: Recreate each SageMaker notebook instance with --direct-internet-access Disabled and --subnet-id pointing to a private subnet (use aws sagemaker create-notebook-instance, or Terraform aws_sagemaker_notebook_instance.direct_internet_access = "Disabled"). Provide pip/yum access through VPC endpoints or a NAT gateway.
SAGEMAKER_NOTEBOOK_NO_DIRECT_INTERNET_AC.title: SageMaker notebook instances must disable direct internet access

SECRETSMANAGER_ROTATION_ENABLED_CHECK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Secrets Manager secrets whose RotationEnabled is false, and (when supplied) whose RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays exceeds maximumAllowedRotationFrequency or whose hourly schedule exceeds maximumAllowedRotationFrequencyInHours.
SECRETSMANAGER_ROTATION_ENABLED_CHECK.condition_logic: secret.RotationEnabled == true AND (maximumAllowedRotationFrequency == null OR secret.RotationRules.AutomaticallyAfterDays <= maximumAllowedRotationFrequency) AND (maximumAllowedRotationFrequencyInHours == null OR secret.RotationRules.ScheduleHours <= maximumAllowedRotationFrequencyInHours)
SECRETSMANAGER_ROTATION_ENABLED_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Secrets Manager secret has rotation enabled. The rule also checks an optional maximumAllowedRotationFrequency parameter. If the parameter is specified, the rotation frequency of the secret is compared with the maximum allowed frequency. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the secret is not scheduled for rotation. The rule is also NON_COMPLIANT if the rotation frequency is higher than the number specified in the maximumAllowedRotationFrequency parameter.
SECRETSMANAGER_ROTATION_ENABLED_CHECK.remediation_summary: Enable automatic rotation on each secret. Use aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <arn> --rotation-lambda-arn <arn> --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30, or Terraform aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation with rotation_lambda_arn and rotation_rules.automatically_after_days. Provide a rotation Lambda function compatible with the secret type.
SECRETSMANAGER_ROTATION_ENABLED_CHECK.title: Secrets Manager secrets must have automatic rotation enabled

SECRETSMANAGER_SCHEDULED_ROTATION_SUCCES.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Secrets Manager secret whose NextRotationDate has passed without LastRotatedDate updating. Secrets without rotation configured are NOT_APPLICABLE.
SECRETSMANAGER_SCHEDULED_ROTATION_SUCCES.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Secrets Manager secrets rotated successfully according to the rotation schedule. Secrets Manager calculates the date the rotation should happen. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the date passes and the secret isn't rotated.
SECRETSMANAGER_SCHEDULED_ROTATION_SUCCES.remediation_summary: Investigate the rotation Lambda function for failures (CloudWatch Logs of the rotation function), fix permissions or logic, and trigger an immediate rotation via aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <arn>. Update Terraform aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation if the rotation_lambda_arn or rotation_rules need correction.
SECRETSMANAGER_SCHEDULED_ROTATION_SUCCES.title: Secrets Manager secrets must rotate on schedule

SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_PERIODIC_ROTATION.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails Secrets Manager secrets whose LastRotatedDate is older than maxDaysSinceRotation (default 90).
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_PERIODIC_ROTATION.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Secrets Manager secrets have been rotated in the past specified number of days. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a secret has not been rotated for more than maxDaysSinceRotation number of days. The default value is 90 days.
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_PERIODIC_ROTATION.remediation_summary: Rotate stale secrets via aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <arn> --rotation-lambda-arn <arn> --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=<n>, then make sure rotation is automated (Terraform aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation) so future rotations stay within the configured window.
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_PERIODIC_ROTATION.title: Secrets Manager secrets must be rotated within the configured period

SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_UNUSED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails Secrets Manager secrets whose LastAccessedDate is older than unusedForDays (default 90).
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_UNUSED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Secrets Manager secrets have been accessed within a specified number of days. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a secret has not been accessed in 'unusedForDays' number of days. The default value is 90 days.
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_UNUSED.remediation_summary: Identify and delete unused Secrets Manager secrets. Use aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id <arn> --recovery-window-in-days 30 (or --force-delete-without-recovery once verified), or remove the corresponding Terraform aws_secretsmanager_secret resource. Re-issue any still-needed secrets to the workloads that legitimately consume them.
SECRETSMANAGER_SECRET_UNUSED.title: Secrets Manager secrets must not remain unused

SECRETSMANAGER_USING_CMK.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Secrets Manager secrets encrypted with the AWS-managed key 'aws/secretsmanager'. When kmsKeyArns is supplied, the secret's KmsKeyId must be in that list.
SECRETSMANAGER_USING_CMK.condition_logic: secret.KmsKeyId != 'alias/aws/secretsmanager' AND (kmsKeyArns == null OR secret.KmsKeyId in kmsKeyArns)
SECRETSMANAGER_USING_CMK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager are encrypted using the AWS managed key (aws/secretsmanager) or a customer managed key that was created in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The rule is COMPLIANT if a secret is encrypted using a customer managed key. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a secret is encrypted using aws/secretsmanager.
SECRETSMANAGER_USING_CMK.remediation_summary: Recreate or update each secret to use a customer-managed KMS key. Use aws secretsmanager update-secret --secret-id <arn> --kms-key-id <cmk-arn>, or Terraform aws_secretsmanager_secret.kms_key_id pointing at an aws_kms_key resource with appropriate key policy granting secretsmanager.amazonaws.com permissions.
SECRETSMANAGER_USING_CMK.title: Secrets Manager secrets must be encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key

SECURITYHUB_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if AWS Security Hub is not enabled in the region.
SECURITYHUB_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Security Hub is enabled for an AWS Account. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if AWS Security Hub is not enabled.
SECURITYHUB_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable Security Hub via aws securityhub enable-security-hub --enable-default-standards or Terraform aws_securityhub_account. Designate a delegated administrator from your AWS Organizations management account so Security Hub findings can be aggregated centrally, and enable the foundational standards (AWS FSBP, CIS, PCI DSS).
SECURITYHUB_ENABLED.title: AWS Security Hub must be enabled

SECURITY_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION_PROVIDED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the AWS account if it does not have a Security alternate contact configured (name, title, email, phone).
SECURITY_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION_PROVIDED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if you have provided security contact information for your AWS account contacts. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if security contact information within the account is not provided.
SECURITY_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION_PROVIDED.remediation_summary: Provide security contact information via aws account put-alternate-contact --alternate-contact-type SECURITY --name ... --title ... --email-address ... --phone-number ..., or via the Account settings page in the AWS Billing console. Use a monitored mailing list rather than an individual mailbox.
SECURITY_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION_PROVIDED.title: AWS account must publish security contact information

SERVICE_CATALOG_SHARED_WITHIN_ORGANIZATI.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any Service Catalog portfolio share whose Type is ACCOUNT instead of ORGANIZATION / ORGANIZATIONAL_UNIT.
SERVICE_CATALOG_SHARED_WITHIN_ORGANIZATI.condition_logic: every share in service_catalog.Portfolio.Shares : share.Type in ['ORGANIZATION','ORGANIZATIONAL_UNIT']
SERVICE_CATALOG_SHARED_WITHIN_ORGANIZATI.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Service Catalog shares portfolios to an organization (a collection of AWS accounts treated as a single unit) when integration is enabled with AWS Organizations. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the Type value of a share is ACCOUNT.
SERVICE_CATALOG_SHARED_WITHIN_ORGANIZATI.remediation_summary: Replace account-level Service Catalog portfolio shares with organization-level shares. Use aws servicecatalog create-portfolio-share --portfolio-id <id> --organization-node Type=ORGANIZATION,Value=<o-id> after enabling AWS Organizations access in Service Catalog, then revoke the old per-account shares with aws servicecatalog delete-portfolio-share.
SERVICE_CATALOG_SHARED_WITHIN_ORGANIZATI.title: Service Catalog portfolios must be shared via AWS Organizations

SHIELD_DRT_ACCESS.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails the account if Shield Advanced is enabled but no IAM role granting Shield Response Team access has been associated.
SHIELD_DRT_ACCESS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the Shield Response Team (SRT) can access your AWS account. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if AWS Shield Advanced is enabled but the role for SRT access is not configured.
SHIELD_DRT_ACCESS.remediation_summary: Create an IAM role assumable by drt.shield.amazonaws.com with the AWSShieldDRTAccessPolicy attached, then run aws shield associate-drt-role --role-arn <arn>. Optionally grant the SRT access to your S3 logs by associating log buckets via aws shield associate-drt-log-bucket.
SHIELD_DRT_ACCESS.title: AWS Shield Advanced must grant SRT access

SNS_ENCRYPTED_KMS.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails SNS topics whose KmsMasterKeyId is null, or (when kmsKeyIds is supplied) whose KmsMasterKeyId is not in the list of allowed key IDs / aliases / ARNs.
SNS_ENCRYPTED_KMS.condition_logic: sns_topic.KmsMasterKeyId != null AND (kmsKeyIds == null OR sns_topic.KmsMasterKeyId in kmsKeyIds)
SNS_ENCRYPTED_KMS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if SNS topics are encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if an SNS topic is not encrypted with AWS KMS.
SNS_ENCRYPTED_KMS.remediation_summary: Set a KmsMasterKeyId on each SNS topic via aws sns set-topic-attributes --topic-arn <arn> --attribute-name KmsMasterKeyId --attribute-value <kms-key-id>, or Terraform aws_sns_topic.kms_master_key_id. Grant the SNS service principal kms:GenerateDataKey/Decrypt on the key.
SNS_ENCRYPTED_KMS.title: SNS topics must be encrypted with AWS KMS

SNS_TOPIC_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_NOTIFICATION_.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails an SNS topic if it lacks delivery-status logging attributes (e.g., HTTPSuccessFeedbackRoleArn, LambdaSuccessFeedbackRoleArn, etc.) appropriate to its subscribed protocols.
SNS_TOPIC_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_NOTIFICATION_.condition_logic: exists(attr in sns_topic.Attributes where attr.name endswith 'SuccessFeedbackRoleArn' AND attr.value != null) AND exists(attr in sns_topic.Attributes where attr.name endswith 'FailureFeedbackRoleArn' AND attr.value != null)
SNS_TOPIC_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_NOTIFICATION_.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) logging is enabled for the delivery status of notification messages sent to a topic for the endpoints. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the delivery status notification for messages is not enabled.
SNS_TOPIC_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_NOTIFICATION_.remediation_summary: Configure delivery-status logging on each SNS topic via aws sns set-topic-attributes for each protocol's <Protocol>SuccessFeedbackRoleArn / <Protocol>FailureFeedbackRoleArn / <Protocol>SuccessFeedbackSampleRate, or Terraform aws_sns_topic fields like http_success_feedback_role_arn / lambda_failure_feedback_role_arn pointing at an IAM role allowed to write CloudWatch Logs.
SNS_TOPIC_MESSAGE_DELIVERY_NOTIFICATION_.title: SNS topics must enable delivery status logging

SSM_DOCUMENT_NOT_PUBLIC.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any SSM document owned by 'Self' whose AccountSharingInfoList includes the AccountId 'all' (publicly shared).
SSM_DOCUMENT_NOT_PUBLIC.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Systems Manager documents owned by the account are public. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Systems Manager documents with the owner 'Self' are public.
SSM_DOCUMENT_NOT_PUBLIC.remediation_summary: Remove public sharing on each SSM document via aws ssm modify-document-permission --name <doc> --permission-type Share --account-ids-to-remove all, or remove the public account_ids entries in Terraform aws_ssm_document. Audit your IaC pipelines to make sure documents are never shared with 'all'.
SSM_DOCUMENT_NOT_PUBLIC.title: SSM documents owned by the account must not be public

STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_LOGGING_ENA.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails Step Functions state machines whose LoggingConfiguration.Level is OFF, whose Level is below logLevel, or (when supplied) whose log group ARN is not in cloudWatchLogGroupArns.
STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_LOGGING_ENA.condition_logic: state_machine.LoggingConfiguration.Level != 'OFF' AND (logLevel == null OR state_machine.LoggingConfiguration.Level == logLevel) AND (cloudWatchLogGroupArns == null OR state_machine.LoggingConfiguration.Destinations[0].CloudWatchLogsLogGroup.LogGroupArn in cloudWatchLogGroupArns)
STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_LOGGING_ENA.framework_control_requirement: Checks if AWS Step Functions machine has logging enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a state machine does not have logging enabled or the logging configuration is not at the minimum level provided.
STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_LOGGING_ENA.remediation_summary: Enable logging on each Step Functions state machine via aws stepfunctions update-state-machine --logging-configuration level=ALL,includeExecutionData=true,destinations=[{cloudWatchLogsLogGroup={logGroupArn=<arn>}}], or Terraform aws_sfn_state_machine.logging_configuration { level = "ALL", include_execution_data = true, log_destination = "<log-group-arn>:*" }.
STEP_FUNCTIONS_STATE_MACHINE_LOGGING_ENA.title: Step Functions state machines must enable logging

SUBNET_AUTO_ASSIGN_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any subnet whose MapPublicIpOnLaunch is true or whose AssignIpv6AddressOnCreation is true with a Global Unicast IPv6 range.
SUBNET_AUTO_ASSIGN_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) subnets are configured to automatically assign public IP addresses to instances launched within them. This rule is COMPLIANT if subnets do not auto-assign public IPv4 or IPv6 addresses. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if subnets auto-assign public IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.
SUBNET_AUTO_ASSIGN_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.remediation_summary: Disable auto-assignment of public IPs on each subnet via aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --subnet-id <id> --no-map-public-ip-on-launch (and --no-assign-ipv6-address-on-creation), or Terraform aws_subnet.map_public_ip_on_launch = false / assign_ipv6_address_on_creation = false. Use explicit public IP allocation only on workloads that require it.
SUBNET_AUTO_ASSIGN_PUBLIC_IP_DISABLED.title: VPC subnets must not auto-assign public IP addresses

TRANSFER_FAMILY_SERVER_NO_FTP.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any Transfer Family server whose Protocols list includes 'FTP' (cleartext file transfer).
TRANSFER_FAMILY_SERVER_NO_FTP.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a server created with AWS Transfer Family uses FTP for endpoint connection. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the server protocol for endpoint connection is FTP-enabled.
TRANSFER_FAMILY_SERVER_NO_FTP.remediation_summary: Migrate Transfer Family servers off plaintext FTP onto SFTP or FTPS. Recreate the server with --protocols SFTP (or FTPS) via aws transfer create-server, or change Terraform aws_transfer_server.protocols = ["SFTP"] / ["FTPS"]. Issue new SSH keys / TLS certificates and update partner integrations to the new endpoint.
TRANSFER_FAMILY_SERVER_NO_FTP.title: AWS Transfer Family servers must not use FTP

VPC_DEFAULT_SECURITY_GROUP_CLOSED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any default security group (GroupName == 'default') with any IpPermissions or IpPermissionsEgress entries.
VPC_DEFAULT_SECURITY_GROUP_CLOSED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if the default security group of any Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) does not allow inbound or outbound traffic. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the default security group has one or more inbound or outbound traffic rules.
VPC_DEFAULT_SECURITY_GROUP_CLOSED.remediation_summary: Remove all inbound and outbound rules from each VPC's default security group via aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress / revoke-security-group-egress, or use Terraform aws_default_security_group with no ingress/egress blocks. Application workloads should use dedicated security groups, not the default.
VPC_DEFAULT_SECURITY_GROUP_CLOSED.title: Default VPC security groups must allow no traffic

VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any VPC without an active FlowLog covering the configured trafficType (defaults to ALL).
VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED.condition_logic: exists(flow_log in ec2.FlowLogs where flow_log.ResourceId == vpc.VpcId AND flow_log.FlowLogStatus == 'ACTIVE' AND (trafficType == null OR flow_log.TrafficType == trafficType))
VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) flow logs are found and enabled for all Amazon VPCs. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if flow logs are not enabled for at least one Amazon VPC.
VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable VPC flow logs on every VPC via aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type VPC --resource-ids <vpc-id> --traffic-type ALL --log-destination-type cloud-watch-logs --log-group-name <name> --deliver-logs-permission-arn <role>, or Terraform aws_flow_log per VPC pointing at a CloudWatch Logs group or S3 bucket.
VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED.title: VPC flow logs must be enabled

VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK.condition_description: Checks if there are unused network access control lists (network ACLs). The rule is COMPLIANT if each network ACL is associated with a subnet. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a network ACL is not associated with a subnet. Identifier: VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::EC2::NetworkAcl Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: None
VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK.framework_control_requirement: Checks if there are unused network access control lists (network ACLs). The rule is COMPLIANT if each network ACL is associated with a subnet. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a network ACL is not associated with a subnet. Identifier: VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK Resource Types: AWS::EC2::NetworkAcl Trigger type: Configuration changes AWS Region: All supported AWS regions Parameters: None
VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK.remediation_summary: Configure the resource to satisfy the rule VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK. See the AWS Config developer guide for the rule for parameter details and specific remediation steps.
VPC_NETWORK_ACL_UNUSED_CHECK.title: Vpc Network Acl Unused Check

VPC_SG_OPEN_ONLY_TO_AUTHORIZED_PORTS.condition_description: Configuration-change and periodic rule that fails any security group with an inbound rule open to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on a TCP or UDP port not listed in authorizedTcpPorts / authorizedUdpPorts.
VPC_SG_OPEN_ONLY_TO_AUTHORIZED_PORTS.condition_logic: every rule in sg.IpPermissions where rule.IpRanges contains '0.0.0.0/0' OR rule.Ipv6Ranges contains '::/0' : (rule.IpProtocol == 'tcp' AND rule.FromPort in authorizedTcpPorts) OR (rule.IpProtocol == 'udp' AND rule.FromPort in authorizedUdpPorts)
VPC_SG_OPEN_ONLY_TO_AUTHORIZED_PORTS.framework_control_requirement: Checks if security groups allowing unrestricted incoming traffic ('0.0.0.0/0' or '::/0') only allow inbound TCP or UDP connections on authorized ports. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if such security groups do not have ports specified in the rule parameters.
VPC_SG_OPEN_ONLY_TO_AUTHORIZED_PORTS.remediation_summary: Restrict 0.0.0.0/0 ingress on each security group to a small set of authorized ports (typically 80, 443). Use aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress to remove unauthorized rules and aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress to recreate scoped rules; in Terraform, refactor aws_security_group ingress blocks to reference allowlisted CIDRs / prefix lists rather than 0.0.0.0/0.
VPC_SG_OPEN_ONLY_TO_AUTHORIZED_PORTS.title: Internet-facing security groups must only allow authorized ports

VPC_VPN_2_TUNNELS_UP.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails a Site-to-Site VPN connection if any of its VgwTelemetry entries reports a tunnel status other than UP.
VPC_VPN_2_TUNNELS_UP.framework_control_requirement: Checks if both virtual private network (VPN) tunnels provided by AWS Site-to-Site VPN are in UP status. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if one or both tunnels are in DOWN status.
VPC_VPN_2_TUNNELS_UP.remediation_summary: Investigate and restore the down VPN tunnel: validate customer-gateway BGP / IKE configuration, refresh shared secrets, and consider using AWS-provided tunnel parameters (aws ec2 modify-vpn-tunnel-options). Alarm on VPN tunnel state via CloudWatch (TunnelState metric) and configure a redundant on-prem device to keep both tunnels active.
VPC_VPN_2_TUNNELS_UP.title: Site-to-Site VPN connections must keep both tunnels UP

WAFV2_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule that fails any WAFv2 Web ACL whose LoggingConfiguration is missing or whose LogDestinationConfigs does not include a Kinesis Firehose ARN listed in KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns when supplied.
WAFV2_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: wafv2_webacl.LoggingConfiguration != null AND (KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns == null OR wafv2_webacl.LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs intersects KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns)
WAFV2_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if logging is enabled on AWS WAFv2 regional and global web access control lists (web ACLs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the logging is enabled but the logging destination does not match the value of the parameter.
WAFV2_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable logging on each WAFv2 Web ACL via aws wafv2 put-logging-configuration with a Kinesis Data Firehose, S3 bucket, or CloudWatch Logs destination, or Terraform aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration.log_destination_configs. Apply matching IAM permissions for the destination.
WAFV2_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: WAFv2 web ACLs must enable logging

WAFV2_RULEGROUP_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails any WAFv2 rule group whose VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled is false. Empty rule groups evaluate as NOT_APPLICABLE.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if Amazon CloudWatch security metrics collection on AWS WAFv2 rule groups is enabled. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if the 'VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled' field is set to false.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable CloudWatch metric collection on each WAFv2 rule group's VisibilityConfig (CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true, MetricName set, SampledRequestsEnabled=true). Apply via aws wafv2 update-rule-group, or Terraform aws_wafv2_rule_group.visibility_config { cloudwatch_metrics_enabled = true, metric_name = ..., sampled_requests_enabled = true }.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: WAFv2 rule groups must enable CloudWatch metric logging

WAFV2_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails WAFv2 rule groups whose Rules list is empty.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if WAFv2 Rule Groups contain rules. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are no rules in a WAFv2 Rule Group.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Add at least one rule to each WAFv2 rule group, or delete unused groups. Use aws wafv2 update-rule-group --rules <json> or Terraform aws_wafv2_rule_group.rule blocks (e.g., a managed rule statement or rate-based rule). Empty rule groups offer no protection and add billing cost.
WAFV2_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.title: WAFv2 rule groups must contain at least one rule

WAFV2_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule that fails WAFv2 Web ACLs whose Rules array is empty (no individual rules and no referenced rule groups).
WAFV2_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if a WAFv2 Web ACL contains any WAF rules or WAF rule groups. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a Web ACL does not contain any WAF rules or WAF rule groups.
WAFV2_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Associate WAFv2 rule groups (e.g., AWS Managed Rules - Common Rule Set, Known Bad Inputs) or custom rules with each Web ACL. Apply via aws wafv2 update-web-acl --rules <json>, or Terraform aws_wafv2_web_acl.rule blocks referencing managed_rule_group_statement / rate_based_statement.
WAFV2_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.title: WAFv2 web ACLs must contain at least one rule or rule group

WAF_CLASSIC_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_description: Periodic rule (us-east-1 only) that fails any WAF Classic global Web ACL without a LoggingConfiguration, or whose LogDestinationConfigs does not include a Firehose ARN listed in KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns when supplied.
WAF_CLASSIC_LOGGING_ENABLED.condition_logic: waf_classic_webacl.LoggingConfiguration != null AND (KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns == null OR waf_classic_webacl.LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs intersects KinesisFirehoseDeliveryStreamArns)
WAF_CLASSIC_LOGGING_ENABLED.framework_control_requirement: Checks if logging is enabled on AWS WAF classic global web access control lists (web ACLs). The rule is NON_COMPLIANT for a global web ACL, if it does not have logging enabled.
WAF_CLASSIC_LOGGING_ENABLED.remediation_summary: Enable logging on each WAF Classic global Web ACL via aws waf put-logging-configuration --logging-configuration ResourceArn=<webacl>,LogDestinationConfigs=<firehose-arn>. Where possible, migrate from WAF Classic to WAFv2 (aws_wafv2_web_acl) and set up wafv2 logging instead.
WAF_CLASSIC_LOGGING_ENABLED.title: WAF Classic global web ACLs must enable logging

WAF_GLOBAL_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (us-east-1 only) that fails any WAF Classic global rule group whose Rules array is empty.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS WAF Classic rule group contains any rules. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if there are no rules present within a rule group.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Add at least one rule to each WAF Classic global rule group, or delete unused groups. Use aws waf update-rule-group --rule-group-id <id> --updates Action=INSERT,ActivatedRule=... or migrate to WAFv2 (aws_wafv2_rule_group) which is the supported product for new deployments.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULEGROUP_NOT_EMPTY.title: WAF Classic global rule groups must contain at least one rule

WAF_GLOBAL_RULE_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (us-east-1 only) that fails any WAF Classic global rule whose Predicates list is empty.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULE_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks if an AWS WAF global rule contains any conditions. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if no conditions are present within the WAF global rule.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULE_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Add at least one Predicate to each WAF Classic global rule via aws waf update-rule --rule-id <id> --updates Action=INSERT,Predicate=..., or remove unused rules. Long-term, migrate to WAFv2 statements (aws_wafv2_web_acl) which provides richer condition types.
WAF_GLOBAL_RULE_NOT_EMPTY.title: WAF Classic global rules must contain at least one condition

WAF_GLOBAL_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.condition_description: Configuration-change rule (us-east-1 only) that fails any WAF Classic global Web ACL whose Rules array is empty.
WAF_GLOBAL_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.framework_control_requirement: Checks whether a WAF Global Web ACL contains any WAF rules or rule groups. This rule is NON_COMPLIANT if a Web ACL does not contain any WAF rule or rule group.
WAF_GLOBAL_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.remediation_summary: Attach at least one WAF Classic rule or rule group to each global Web ACL via aws waf update-web-acl --web-acl-id <id> --updates Action=INSERT,ActivatedRule=..., or move the workload behind a WAFv2 Web ACL (aws_wafv2_web_acl) with managed rule groups.
WAF_GLOBAL_WEBACL_NOT_EMPTY.title: WAF Classic global web ACLs must contain at least one rule
